And this is the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which we used to pray with him.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik related to me. He said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray ‘Asr while the sun was high and bright. A person would go to al-‘Awali and reach them while the sun was still high. Some of al-‘Awali are four miles from Madinah, or thereabouts.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

We used to pray ‘Asr. Then one of us would go to Quba’ and reach them while the sun was still high.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The one who misses the ‘Asr prayer is as though he has been deprived of his family and his wealth.”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Malih, who said:

We were with Buraydah on an expedition on a cloudy day. He said: “Pray ‘Asr early, for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever leaves the ‘Asr prayer, his work has come to nothing.’”

Al-Humaydi related to us. He said: Marwan ibn Mu‘awiyah related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us, from Qays, from Jarir, who said:

We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he looked at the moon one night—meaning the full moon—and said: “You will indeed see your Lord as you see this moon, without suffering harm in seeing Him. If you can avoid being overcome and missing a prayer before the sun rises and before it sets, then do so.” Then he recited: “And glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before the setting.”

Isma‘il said: “Do so; do not let it escape you.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik related to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Angels take turns among you by night and angels by day, and they gather at the Fajr prayer and the ‘Asr prayer. Then those who spent the night among you ascend, and He asks them—though He knows them better—‘How did you leave My servants?’ They say: ‘We left them while they were praying, and we came to them while they were praying.’”

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“If one of you catches a prostration of the ‘Asr prayer before the sun sets, let him complete his prayer. And if he catches a prostration of the morning prayer before the sun rises, let him complete his prayer.”

‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah, from his father, who informed him that he heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“Your remaining duration, compared with the nations that came before you, is only like the interval between the ‘Asr prayer and sunset. The people of the Torah were given the Torah and worked until midday, when they were unable to continue, and were given a qirat each. Then the people of the Gospel were given the Gospel and worked until the ‘Asr prayer, when they were unable to continue, and were given a qirat each. Then we were given the Qur’an and worked until sunset, and were given two qirats each. The people of the two Books said: ‘Our Lord, You gave these two qirats each and gave us one qirat each, although we did more work.’” He said: “Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ‘Have I wronged you in any part of your wages?’ They said: ‘No.’ He said: ‘It is My favour; I give it to whomever I will.’”

Abu Kurayb related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“The likeness of the Muslims, the Jews and the Christians is that of a man who hired some people to do work for him until night. They worked until midday, then said: ‘We have no need of your wages.’ He hired others and said: ‘Complete the rest of your day, and you will have what I stipulated.’ They worked until the time of the ‘Asr prayer, then said: ‘What we have done is yours.’ He hired some people who worked for the rest of their day until the sun set, and they received the full wages of both groups.”

Muhammad ibn Mihran related to us. He said: Al-Walid related to us. He said: Al-Awza‘i related to us. He said: Abu al-Najashi, ‘Ata’ ibn Suhayb, the freedman of Rafi‘ ibn Khadij, related to us. He said: I heard Rafi‘ ibn Khadij say:

We used to pray Maghrib with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one of us would leave while he could still see where his arrows fell.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Sa‘d, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali, who said:

Al-Hajjaj arrived, and we asked Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah. He said: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray Dhuhr in the midday heat, and ‘Asr while the sun was clear, and Maghrib when it set. ‘Isha’ was sometimes at one time and sometimes at another: if he saw that they had gathered, he prayed early; if he saw that they were slow, he delayed it. As for the morning prayer, they used to—or the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to—pray it while it was still dark at dawn.”

Al-Makki ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Abi ‘Ubayd related to us, from Salamah, who said:

We used to pray Maghrib with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when it disappeared behind the veil.

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Dinar related to us. He said: I heard Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed seven together and eight together.

Abu Ma‘mar—he is ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr—related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us, from al-Husayn, who said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Buraydah related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah al-Muzani related to me that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Do not let the Bedouins prevail over you concerning the name of your prayer, Maghrib.”

He said: “The Bedouins call it ‘Isha’.”

‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah informed us. He said: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim said: ‘Abd Allah informed me:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us one night in the ‘Isha’ prayer, which the people call al-‘Atamah. Then he turned away and faced us, saying: “Consider this night of yours: at the end of a hundred years from it, none of those who are on the face of the earth will remain.”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr—he is the son of al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali—who said:

We asked Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah about the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: “He used to pray Dhuhr in the midday heat, and ‘Asr while the sun was bright, and Maghrib when it set. For ‘Isha’, if the people were numerous he prayed early, and if they were few he delayed it; and he prayed the morning prayer while it was still dark at dawn.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, that ‘A’ishah informed him. She said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed ‘Isha’ one night, before Islam had spread. He did not come out until ‘Umar said: “The women and children have fallen asleep.” He came out and said to the people in the mosque: “No one on earth is waiting for it except you.”

Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ related to us. He said: Abu Usamah informed us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said:

My companions who had come with me on the ship and I were staying in Baqi‘ Buthan, while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was in Madinah. Each night a group of them took turns visiting the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at the ‘Isha’ prayer. My companions and I came upon the Prophet, peace be upon him, when he was occupied with some matter of his, and he delayed the prayer until the night had grown deep. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out and led them in prayer. When he finished his prayer, he said to those present: “Wait. Rejoice: among Allah’s favours to you is that no one else is praying at this hour except you”—or he said: “No one has prayed at this hour except you.”

He did not know which of the two expressions he said.

He said: Abu Musa said: “We returned, rejoicing at what we had heard from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Muhammad ibn Salam related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi informed us. He said: Khalid al-Hadhdha’ related to us, from Abu al-Minhal, from Abu Barzah:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, disliked sleeping before ‘Isha’ and conversation after it.

Ayyub ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Abu Bakr related to me, from Sulayman, who said: Salih ibn Kaysan said: Ibn Shihab informed me, from ‘Urwah, that ‘A’ishah said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed ‘Isha’ until ‘Umar called to him: “The prayer! The women and children have fallen asleep.” He came out and said: “No one on earth is waiting for it except you.”

He said: “At that time it was only prayed in Madinah. They used to pray between the disappearance of twilight and the first third of the night.”

Mahmud related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed me. He said: Nafi‘ informed me. He said: ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to us:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was occupied one night and delayed it until we fell asleep in the mosque, then awoke, then fell asleep, then awoke. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to us and said: “No one on earth is waiting for the prayer except you.”

Ibn ‘Umar did not mind whether he prayed it early or delayed it, provided he did not fear that sleep would overcome him and cause him to miss its time. He used to sleep before it.

Ibn Jurayj said: I said to ‘Ata’, and he said: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas say:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed ‘Isha’ one night until the people fell asleep and awoke, and fell asleep and awoke. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: “The prayer!” ‘Ata’ said: Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out—as though I were looking at him now—with water dripping from his head and his hand resting on it. He said: “Were it not that I would cause hardship to my community, I would command them to pray it like this.”

I asked ‘Ata’ to confirm how the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had placed his hand on his head, as Ibn ‘Abbas had informed him. ‘Ata’ spread his fingers apart a little for me, then placed his fingertips on the side of his head. Then he brought them together, drawing them across his head like that until his thumb touched the edge of his ear next to his face, at the temple and towards the beard, neither slowing down nor hurrying, but just like that. And he said: “Were it not that I would cause hardship to my community, I would command them to pray like this.”

‘Abd al-Rahim al-Muharibi related to us. He said: Za’idah related to us, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed the ‘Isha’ prayer until the middle of the night, then prayed. Then he said: “The people have prayed and slept. As for you, you remain in prayer as long as you wait for it.”

And Ibn Abi Maryam added: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us. Humayd related to me that he heard Anas:

“It is as though I were looking at the gleam of his ring that night.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Isma‘il. Qays related to us. He said: Jarir ibn ‘Abd Allah said to me:

We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: “You will indeed see your Lord as you see this. You will not suffer harm—or you will not be in doubt—in seeing Him. If you can avoid being overcome and missing a prayer before the sun rises and before it sets, then do so.” Then he said: “So glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting.”

Hudbah ibn Khalid related to us. He said: Hammam related to us. Abu Jamrah related to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Musa, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever prays the two cool prayers will enter the Garden.”

And Ibn Raja’ said: Hammam related to us, from Abu Jamrah, that Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Qays informed him of this.

Ishaq related to us, from Hibban. Hammam related to us. Abu Jamrah related to us, from Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd Allah, from his father, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with the like of it.

‘Amr ibn ‘Asim related to us. He said: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, that Zayd ibn Thabit related to him:

They ate the pre-dawn meal with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then stood up for prayer. I said: “How much time was between the two?” He said: “The amount of fifty or sixty,”

meaning verses.

Hasan ibn Sabbah related to us. He heard Rawh: Sa‘id related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik:

That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Zayd ibn Thabit ate the pre-dawn meal. When they had finished their pre-dawn meal, the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up for prayer and prayed. We said to Anas: “How long was it between their finishing their pre-dawn meal and their beginning the prayer?” He said: “The time in which a man recites fifty verses.”

Isma‘il ibn Abi Uways related to us, from his brother, from Sulayman, from Abu Hazim, that he heard Sahl ibn Sa‘d say:

I used to eat the pre-dawn meal with my family, then hurry so that I could catch the Fajr prayer with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth informed us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab. He said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘A’ishah informed him. She said:

The believing women used to attend the Fajr prayer with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wrapped in their garments. Then they would return to their homes when they had finished the prayer, and no one would recognise them because of the darkness at dawn.

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, and from Busr ibn Sa‘id, and from al-A‘raj—they related to him from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever catches a rak‘ah of the morning prayer before the sun rises has caught the morning prayer, and whoever catches a rak‘ah of ‘Asr before the sun sets has caught ‘Asr.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever catches a rak‘ah of the prayer has caught the prayer.”

Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-‘Aliyah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

Men whom I trusted testified before me—and the one I trusted most among them was ‘Umar—that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade prayer after the morning prayer until the sun rises, and after ‘Asr until it sets.
Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Shu‘bah, from Qatadah: I heard Abu al-‘Aliyah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Some people related to me about this.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from Hisham, who said: My father informed me. He said: Ibn ‘Umar informed me. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Do not seek out sunrise or sunset for your prayer.”

And he said: Ibn ‘Umar related to me. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When the edge of the sun appears, delay the prayer until it rises higher; and when the edge of the sun disappears, delay the prayer until it disappears completely.”

‘Abdah corroborated him.

‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us, from Abu Usamah, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Khubayb ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn ‘Asim, from Abu Hurayrah:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade two kinds of sale, two ways of dressing and two prayers. He forbade prayer after Fajr until the sun rises, and after ‘Asr until the sun sets; ishtimal al-samma’; sitting in ihtiba’ in a single garment with one’s private parts exposed towards the sky; and munabadhah and mulamasah.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“None of you should seek out the time of sunrise or sunset to pray.”

‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid al-Junda‘i informed me that he heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“There is no prayer after the morning prayer until the sun rises higher, and there is no prayer after ‘Asr until the sun sets.”

Muhammad ibn Aban related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, who said: I heard Humran ibn Aban relating from Mu‘awiyah, who said:

“You are indeed praying a prayer! We accompanied the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and never saw him pray it, and he forbade the two,”

meaning the two rak‘ahs after ‘Asr.

Muhammad ibn Salam related to us. He said: ‘Abdah related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Khubayb, from Hafs ibn ‘Asim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade two prayers: after Fajr until the sun rises, and after ‘Asr until the sun sets.

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said:

“I pray as I saw my companions pray. I do not forbid anyone to pray at night or by day as much as he wishes, except that you should not seek out sunrise or sunset.”

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Ayman related to us. He said: My father related to me that he heard ‘A’ishah say:

“By the One who took him away, he never left them until he met Allah. He did not meet Allah, exalted is He, until prayer had become burdensome for him, and he used to perform many of his prayers sitting,”

she means the two rak‘ahs after ‘Asr.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray them, but he did not pray them in the mosque for fear of burdening his community, and he loved what made things easier for them.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: My father informed me: ‘A’ishah said:

“Son of my sister, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, never left the two prostrations after ‘Asr with me.”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: Al-Shaybani related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad related to us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

“Two rak‘ahs that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would not leave, in private or in public: two rak‘ahs before the morning prayer and two rak‘ahs after ‘Asr.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Ar‘arah related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I saw al-Aswad and Masruq testify concerning ‘A’ishah that she said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, never came to me on a day after ‘Asr without praying two rak‘ahs.

Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya—he is Ibn Abi Kathir—from Abu Qilabah, that Abu al-Malih related to him. He said:

We were with Buraydah on a cloudy day, and he said: “Pray early, for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever leaves the ‘Asr prayer, his work has come to nothing.’”

‘Imran ibn Maysarah related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us. He said: Husayn related to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said:

We travelled with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, one night. Some of the people said: “If only you would stop for us to rest, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “I fear that you will sleep through the prayer.” Bilal said: “I will wake you.” They lay down, and Bilal rested his back against his mount. His eyes overcame him and he slept. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, awoke when the edge of the sun had appeared. He said: “Bilal, where is what you said?” He said: “Never has sleep like this come upon me.” He said: “Allah took your souls when He wished and returned them to you when He wished. Bilal, get up and call the people to prayer.” He performed ablution, and when the sun had risen higher and become bright, he stood up and prayed.

Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah:

That ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab came on the day of the Ditch after the sun had set and began cursing the unbelievers of Quraysh. He said: “Messenger of Allah, I barely managed to pray ‘Asr before the sun was about to set.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “By Allah, I have not prayed it.” We got up and went to Buthan. He performed ablution for the prayer, and we performed ablution for it. He prayed ‘Asr after the sun had set, then prayed Maghrib after it.

Abu Nu‘aym and Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. They said: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray when he remembers it. There is no expiation for it except that.”

“And establish the prayer for My remembrance.”

Musa said: Hammam said: I heard him later saying: “And establish the prayer for remembrance.”

And Habban said: Hammam related to us. Qatadah related to us. Anas related to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the like of it.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Hisham, who said: Yahya—he is Ibn Abi Kathir—related to us, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir, who said:

‘Umar began cursing their unbelievers on the day of the Ditch, and said: “I could hardly pray ‘Asr until it set.” He said: “We went down to Buthan, and he prayed after the sun had set, then prayed Maghrib.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: ‘Awf related to us. He said: Abu al-Minhal related to us. He said:

I went with my father to Abu Barzah al-Aslami. My father said to him: “Tell us how the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the prescribed prayer.” He said: “He used to pray the midday prayer—which you call the first—when the sun declined, and he prayed ‘Asr, then one of us would return to his family in the furthest part of Madinah while the sun was bright.”

And I have forgotten what he said about Maghrib.

He said: “He liked to delay ‘Isha’.” He said: “He disliked sleeping before it and conversation after it. He used to finish the morning prayer when one of us could recognise the person sitting beside him, and he would recite from sixty to a hundred.”

‘Abd Allah ibn al-Sabbah related to us. He said: Abu ‘Ali al-Hanafi related to us. Qurrah ibn Khalid related to us. He said:

We waited for al-Hasan, and he was late in coming to us until we were close to his time for rising. He came and said: “These neighbours of ours invited us.”

Then he said: Anas said:

We waited for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, one night until it was approaching half the night. He came and led us in prayer, then addressed us, saying: “Indeed, the people have prayed and then gone to sleep, while you have continued in prayer as long as you have waited for the prayer.”

Al-Hasan said: “People continue to be in good as long as they wait for good.”

Qurrah said: “It is from Anas’s hadith from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Hathmah related to me that ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed ‘Isha’ near the end of his life. When he had given the greeting of peace, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up and said: “Consider this night of yours: at the end of a hundred, no one who is on the face of the earth today will remain.” The people misunderstood the statement of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, taking it to mean what they say in these accounts about a hundred years. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, only said: “No one who is on the face of the earth today will remain,” intending by that the passing away of that generation.

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Mu‘tamir ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: My father related to us. Abu ‘Uthman related to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr:

That the people of the Suffah were poor people, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever has food for two should take a third, and if for four, then a fifth or a sixth.” Abu Bakr brought three, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went off with ten. He said: “It was I, my father and my mother,”

I do not know whether he said: “And my wife and a servant shared between us and Abu Bakr’s household.”

Abu Bakr ate supper with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then remained where ‘Isha’ was prayed. Then he returned and stayed until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ate supper. He came after as much of the night had passed as Allah wished. His wife said to him: “What kept you from your guests?”—or she said: “Your guest.” He said: “Did you not give them supper?” She said: “They refused until you came. It was offered to them, but they refused.” He said: “I went and hid.” He said: “Ghunthar!” Then he invoked mutilation against me and insulted me, and said: “Eat, without enjoyment!” He said: “By Allah, I will never eat it.” By Allah, whenever we took a morsel, more than it grew from beneath it.

He said, meaning: until they were full and it had become more than it was before.

Abu Bakr looked at it, and it was as it had been, or more. He said to his wife: “Sister of Banu Firas, what is this?” She said: “No, by the joy of my eye, it is now three times more than it was before.” Abu Bakr ate some of it and said: “That was only from Satan,”

meaning his oath.

Then he ate a morsel of it and carried it to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and it remained with him until morning. There was an agreement between us and some people, and its term expired. He divided us among twelve men, with people accompanying each of them—Allah knows how many were with each man—and they all ate from it,

or as he said.

‘Imran ibn Maysarah related to us. ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. Khalid al-Hadhdha’ related to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, who said:

They mentioned fire and the bell, and mentioned the Jews and the Christians. Bilal was then ordered to say the adhan in pairs and the iqamah singly.

Mahmud ibn Ghaylan related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us. He said: Nafi‘ informed me that Ibn ‘Umar used to say:

When the Muslims arrived in Madinah, they would gather and estimate the time of prayer; no call was made for it. One day they discussed this. Some of them said: “Use a bell like the Christians’ bell.” Others said: “Rather, a trumpet like the Jews’ horn.” ‘Umar said: “Will you not send a man to call to prayer?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Bilal, stand up and call to prayer.”

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Simak ibn ‘Atiyyah, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, who said:

Bilal was ordered to say the adhan in pairs and the iqamah singly, except the iqamah.

Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab informed us. He said: Khalid al-Hadhdha’ informed us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

When the people became numerous—he said—they discussed making the time of prayer known by something they would recognize. They mentioned lighting a fire or striking a bell. Bilal was then ordered to say the adhan in pairs and the iqamah singly.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim related to us. Khalid related to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, who said:

Bilal was ordered to say the adhan in pairs and the iqamah singly.

Isma‘il said: I mentioned this to Ayyub, and he said: “Except the iqamah.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the call to prayer is made, Satan turns away, passing wind, so that he does not hear the adhan. When the call is finished, he returns. Then, when the iqamah is called for prayer, he turns away. When the iqamah is finished, he returns, coming between a person and his own self, saying: ‘Remember such-and-such; remember such-and-such,’ about things he had not been remembering, until the man no longer knows how much he has prayed.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa‘sa‘ah al-Ansari, then al-Mazini, from his father, who informed him that Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri said to him:

“I see that you love sheep and the open country. When you are among your sheep or in your open country and give the call to prayer, raise your voice in the call. No jinn, human, or anything else that hears the reach of the caller’s voice will fail to bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection.”

Abu Sa‘id said: I heard this from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik:

That when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went on an expedition with us against a people, he would not attack them with us until morning, when he would observe. If he heard an adhan, he held back from them; if he did not hear an adhan, he raided them. He said: We went out to Khaybar and reached them at night. When morning came and he heard no adhan, he mounted, and I rode behind Abu Talhah; my foot was touching the Prophet’s foot, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: They came out towards us with their baskets and spades. When they saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, they said: “Muhammad! By Allah, Muhammad and the army!” He said: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw them, he said: “Allah is greatest! Allah is greatest! Khaybar is ruined. When we descend upon a people’s courtyard, evil is the morning of those who have been warned.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid al-Laythi, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When you hear the call, say the same as the caller says.”

Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith, who said: ‘Isa ibn Talhah related to me:

That he heard Mu‘awiyah one day, and he said the same, up to his words: “And I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.”

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh related to us. He said: Wahb ibn Jarir related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya:

Something similar.

Yahya said: And some of our brothers related to me that he said:

When he said, “Come to prayer,” he said, “There is no power and no strength except through Allah.” And he said: “This is how we heard your Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, speak.”

‘Ali ibn ‘Ayyash related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb ibn Abi Hamzah related to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says, on hearing the call, ‘O Allah, Lord of this complete call and the prayer being established, grant Muhammad al-Wasilah and pre-eminence, and raise him to a praised station which You have promised him,’ my intercession will be due to him on the Day of Resurrection.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Sumayy, the freedman of Abu Bakr, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “If people knew what is in the call and the first row, and then found no way to obtain it except by drawing lots, they would draw lots. If they knew what is in going early, they would race to it. And if they knew what is in ‘Isha’ and the dawn prayer, they would come to them even crawling.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, ‘Abd al-Hamid, the companion of al-Ziyadi, and ‘Asim al-Ahwal, from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, who said:

Ibn ‘Abbas addressed us on a muddy day. When the caller reached “Come to prayer,” he ordered him to call: “Prayer in your dwellings.” The people looked at one another. He said: “Someone better than him did this, and it is an obligation.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah, from his father:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Bilal calls the adhan at night, so eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum makes the call.”

Then he said: He was a blind man who would not make the call until he was told: “Morning has come. Morning has come.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, who said: Hafsah informed me:

That when the caller remained in place for the dawn prayer and dawn had appeared, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would pray two brief rak‘ahs before the prayer was commenced.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from ‘A’ishah:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray two brief rak‘ahs between the call and the iqamah for the dawn prayer.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. Malik informed us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Bilal makes the call at night, so eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum makes the call.”

Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us. He said: Sulayman al-Taymi related to us, from Abu ‘Uthman al-Nahdi, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Mas‘ud, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Let Bilal’s adhan not prevent any one of you—or anyone among you—from his pre-dawn meal, for he gives the adhan—or calls—at night, so that those of you standing in prayer may return and those of you sleeping may awaken. Dawn—or morning—is not like this”—and he gestured with his fingers, raising them upwards and lowering them downwards—“until it is like this.”

And Zuhayr gestured with his two index fingers, one above the other, then extended them to his right and left.

Ishaq related to us. He said: Abu Usamah informed us. He said: ‘Ubayd Allah related to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from ‘A’ishah, and from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

Another chain: And Yusuf ibn ‘Isa al-Marwazi related to me. He said: al-Fadl related to us. He said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from ‘A’ishah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said:

“Bilal gives the adhan at night, so eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum gives the adhan.”

Ishaq al-Wasiti related to us. He said: Khalid related to us, from al-Jurayri, from Ibn Buraydah, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Between every two calls there is a prayer”—three times—“for whoever wishes.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: I heard ‘Amr ibn ‘Amir al-Ansari, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

When the caller gave the adhan, some Companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would stand and hurry towards the pillars, until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out while they were like that, praying the two rak‘ahs before Maghrib. There was no interval between the adhan and the iqamah.

‘Uthman ibn Jabalah and Abu Dawud said, from Shu‘bah: There was only a little between them.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘A’ishah said:

When the caller fell silent after the first call for the dawn prayer, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would stand and pray two brief rak‘ahs before the dawn prayer, after dawn had become clear. Then he would lie on his right side until the caller came to him for the iqamah.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yazid related to us. He said: Kahmas ibn al-Hasan related to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Between every two calls there is a prayer. Between every two calls there is a prayer.” Then he said on the third occasion: “For whoever wishes.”

Mu‘alla ibn Asad related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Malik ibn al-Huwayrith:

I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with a group from my people, and we stayed with him for twenty nights. He was merciful and gentle. When he saw our longing for our families, he said: “Return and stay among them, teach them, and pray. When the time for prayer comes, let one of you give the adhan for you, and let the oldest of you lead you.”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Muhajir Abu al-Hasan, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abu Dharr, who said:

We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a journey. The caller wanted to give the adhan, but he told him: “Wait until it is cooler.” Then he wanted to give the adhan, but he told him: “Wait until it is cooler.” Then he wanted to give the adhan, but he told him: “Wait until it is cooler,” until the shadow equalled the hillocks. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The intensity of the heat is from the blast of Hell.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha’, from Abu Qilabah, from Malik ibn al-Huwayrith, who said:

Two men came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, intending to travel. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When you two set out, give the adhan, then the iqamah, then let the older of you lead you.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from Abu Qilabah, who said: Malik related to us:

We came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as young men close in age, and stayed with him for twenty days and nights. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was merciful and gentle. When he thought that we had begun to long for our families—or yearn for them—he asked us about those we had left behind, and we told him. He said: “Return to your families, stay among them, teach them, and instruct them.”

And he mentioned things which I remember—or do not remember.

“And pray as you have seen me pray. When the time for prayer comes, let one of you give the adhan for you, and let the oldest of you lead you.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya informed us, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Umar, who said: Nafi‘ related to me. He said:

Ibn ‘Umar gave the adhan on a cold night at Dajnan, then said: “Pray in your dwellings.” He informed us that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to order a caller to give the adhan, then say immediately afterwards: “Pray in the dwellings,” on a cold or rainy night during a journey.

Ishaq related to us. He said: Ja‘far ibn ‘Awn informed us. He said: Abu al-‘Umays related to us, from ‘Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from his father, who said:

I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at al-Abtah. Bilal came to him and informed him of the prayer. Then Bilal came out with the short spear and planted it before the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at al-Abtah, and gave the iqamah.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from his father:

That he saw Bilal giving the adhan: I began following his mouth this way and that as he gave the adhan.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said:

While we were praying with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he heard a commotion of men. When he had prayed, he said: “What is the matter with you?” They said: “We hurried to the prayer.” He said: “Do not do that. When you come to prayer, be calm. Pray what you catch, and complete what you have missed.”

Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us. He said: al-Zuhri related to us, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; and from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“When you hear the iqamah, walk to prayer with calmness and dignity, and do not hurry. Pray what you catch, and complete what you have missed.”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: Yahya wrote to me, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When the iqamah has been given, do not stand until you see me.”

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When the iqamah has been given, do not stand until you see me, and remain calm.”

‘Ali ibn al-Mubarak followed him in transmitting this.

‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out after the iqamah had been given and the rows had been straightened. When he stood in his prayer place, we waited for him to say the takbir. He turned back and said: “Stay where you are.” We remained as we were until he came out to us with water dripping from his head; he had bathed.

Ishaq related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: al-Awza‘i related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

The iqamah was given, and the people straightened their rows. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out and went forward while he was in a state of janabah. Then he said: “Stay where you are.” He returned and bathed, then came out with his head dripping water and led them in prayer.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, who said: I heard Abu Salamah say: Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah informed us:

That ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on the Day of the Trench and said: “Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I had scarcely managed to pray before the sun was about to set.” That was after the fasting person had broken his fast. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “By Allah, I have not prayed it.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went down to Buthan, and I was with him. He performed ablution and then prayed—meaning ‘Asr—after the sun had set, then prayed Maghrib after it.

Abu Ma‘mar ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb related to us, from Anas, who said:

The iqamah was given while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was speaking privately to a man at the side of the mosque. He did not stand for prayer until the people had fallen asleep.

‘Ayyash ibn al-Walid related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-A‘la related to us. He said: Humayd related to us.

He said: I asked Thabit al-Bunani about a man speaking after the iqamah had been given. He related to me, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

The iqamah was given, and a man approached the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and detained him after the iqamah had been given.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“By Him in whose hand is my soul, I considered ordering firewood to be gathered, then ordering the prayer and having its adhan called, then ordering a man to lead the people, then going to some men and burning their houses down upon them. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of them knew that he would find a meaty bone or two good pieces of meat from between a sheep’s hooves, he would attend ‘Isha’.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Congregational prayer surpasses the prayer of a person alone by twenty-seven degrees.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth informed us: Ibn al-Had related to me, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Khabbab, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, that he heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“Congregational prayer surpasses the prayer of a person alone by twenty-five degrees.”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: I heard Abu Salih say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“A man’s prayer in congregation is multiplied twenty-five times over his prayer in his house and in his marketplace. That is because, when he performs ablution and performs it well, then goes out to the mosque with nothing taking him out except prayer, he takes no step without being raised a degree by it and having a sin removed from him by it. When he prays, the angels continue to pray for him as long as he is in his place of prayer: ‘O Allah, bless him. O Allah, have mercy on him.’ And one of you continues to be in prayer as long as he waits for prayer.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“Congregational prayer surpasses the prayer of one of you alone by twenty-five parts. The angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the Fajr prayer.”

Then Abu Hurayrah says: “Recite, if you wish: ‘Indeed, the recitation at dawn is witnessed.’”

Shu‘ayb said: And Nafi‘ related to me, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, who said: “It surpasses it by twenty-seven degrees.”

‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. He said: My father related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: I heard Salim say: I heard Umm al-Darda’ say:

Abu al-Darda’ came in to me while he was angry. I said: “What has angered you?” He said: “By Allah, I recognize nothing of the community of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, except that they pray together.”

Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Burayd ibn ‘Abd Allah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Those with the greatest reward for prayer are those who walk the farthest, then the next farthest. One who waits for prayer until he prays it with the imam has a greater reward than one who prays and then sleeps.”

Qutaybah related to us, from Malik, from Sumayy, the freedman of Abu Bakr, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“While a man was walking along a road, he found a thorny branch on the road and moved it aside. Allah appreciated his deed and forgave him.” Then he said: “The martyrs are five: one who dies of plague, one who dies of an abdominal illness, one who drowns, one who dies under a collapsed structure, and one martyred in the path of Allah.” And he said: “If people knew what there is in the call and the first row, then found no way except to draw lots, they would draw lots for it. If they knew what there is in going early, they would race to it. If they knew what there is in ‘Isha’ and the dawn prayer, they would come to them even crawling.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Hawshab related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: Humayd related to us, from Anas, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Banu Salimah, will you not seek reward for your footsteps?”

And Mujahid said concerning His words, “And We record what they have sent ahead and their traces”: He said: “Their footsteps.”

And Ibn Abi Maryam said: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us. Humayd related to me. Anas related to me:

That Banu Salimah wanted to move from their homes and settle near the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, disliked their leaving Madinah deserted, and said: “Will you not seek reward for your footsteps?”

Mujahid said: “Their footsteps are their traces: walking on the earth with their feet.”

‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. He said: My father related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: Abu Salih related to me, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“No prayer is heavier upon the hypocrites than Fajr and ‘Isha’. If they knew what there is in them, they would come to them even crawling. I considered ordering the caller to give the iqamah, then ordering a man to lead the people, then taking flames of fire and setting fire to those who have not yet gone out to prayer.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ related to us. He said: Khalid related to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Malik ibn al-Huwayrith, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“When the time for prayer comes, let the two of you give the adhan and the iqamah, then let the older of you lead you.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The angels pray for one of you as long as he is in his place of prayer and has not broken his ablution: ‘O Allah, forgive him. O Allah, have mercy on him.’ One of you continues to be in prayer as long as prayer detains him, with nothing preventing him from returning to his family except prayer.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, who said: Khubayb ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman related to me, from Hafs ibn ‘Asim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Seven will Allah shade in His shade on a day when there is no shade except His shade: a just imam; a young person who grew up worshipping his Lord; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; two men who loved one another for Allah’s sake, meeting on that basis and parting on that basis; a man whom a woman of rank and beauty sought, who said, ‘I fear Allah’; a man who gave charity and concealed it so that his left hand did not know what his right hand spent; and a man who remembered Allah alone, and his eyes overflowed.”

Qutaybah related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us, from Humayd, who said:

And Anas was asked: “Did the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, have a ring?”

He said: “Yes. One night he delayed the ‘Isha’ prayer until halfway through the night. Then, after he had prayed, he turned his face towards us and said: ‘The people have prayed and slept, and you have continued to be in prayer since you began waiting for it.’” He said: “It is as though I am looking at the gleam of his ring.”

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Mutarrif informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Whoever goes to the mosque in the morning and in the evening, Allah prepares hospitality for him in Paradise each time he goes in the morning or the evening.”

‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from his father, from Hafs ibn ‘Asim, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Malik ibn Buhaynah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by a man.

He said: And ‘Abd al-Rahman related to me. He said: Bahz ibn Asad related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim informed me. He said: I heard Hafs ibn ‘Asim say: I heard a man from al-Azd called Malik ibn Buhaynah say:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw a man praying two rak‘ahs when the iqamah had been given. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had finished, the people gathered around him, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “The dawn prayer as four? The dawn prayer as four?”

Ghundar and Mu‘adh corroborated it from Shu‘bah concerning Malik. And Ibn Ishaq said: From Sa‘d, from Hafs, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Buhaynah. And Hammad said: Sa‘d informed us, from Hafs, from Malik.

‘Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us. He said: My father related to me. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us, from Ibrahim, who said: Al-Aswad said:

We were with ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, and we mentioned constancy in prayer and the great regard due to it. She said: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became ill with the illness in which he died, the time for prayer came and the adhan was given. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” He was told: “Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. If he stands in your place, he will not be able to lead the people in prayer.” He repeated it, and they repeated it to him. He repeated it a third time and said: “You are the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Abu Bakr went out and prayed. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt some relief and went out supported between two men. It is as though I can see his feet dragging from the pain. Abu Bakr wanted to move back, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to him to stay in his place. Then he was brought until he sat beside him.

Al-A‘mash was asked: “Was the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying, with Abu Bakr praying following his prayer, and the people praying following Abu Bakr’s prayer?” He nodded yes.

Abu Dawud related part of it from Shu‘bah, from al-A‘mash. Abu Mu‘awiyah added: “He sat to Abu Bakr’s left, and Abu Bakr prayed standing.”

Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us. He said: Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us, from Ma‘mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah informed me. He said: ‘A’ishah said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became seriously ill and his pain intensified, he asked his wives’ permission to be cared for in my house, and they gave him permission. He went out between two men, his feet dragging on the ground. He was between al-‘Abbas and another man.

‘Ubayd Allah said: I mentioned to Ibn ‘Abbas what ‘A’ishah had said. He said to me: “Do you know who the man was whom ‘A’ishah did not name?” I said: “No.” He said: “He was ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘:

That Ibn ‘Umar gave the adhan for prayer on a cold, windy night. Then he said: “Listen, pray in your dwellings.” Then he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to instruct the caller, when it was a cold, rainy night, to say: ‘Listen, pray in your dwellings.’”

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ al-Ansari:

That ‘Itban ibn Malik used to lead his people in prayer, and he was blind. He said to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Messenger of Allah, there is darkness and floodwater, and I am a man with impaired sight. Pray, Messenger of Allah, in a place in my house that I can take as a place of prayer.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to him and said: “Where would you like me to pray?” He pointed to a place in the house, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed there.

‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Hamid, the companion of al-Ziyadi, related to us. He said: I heard ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith say:

Ibn ‘Abbas addressed us on a muddy day. When the caller reached “Come to prayer,” he instructed him, saying: “Say: ‘Prayer in the dwellings.’” Some of them looked at one another, as though they disapproved. He said: “It seems that you disapprove of this. Someone better than me did this”—meaning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. “It is a binding duty, and I disliked putting you in hardship.”

And from Hammad, from ‘Asim, from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn ‘Abbas, something similar, except that he said: “I disliked causing you to incur sin, so that you would come trudging through mud up to your knees.”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, who said:

I asked Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, and he said:

A cloud came and rained until the roof leaked. It was made of palm fronds. The iqamah was given, and I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prostrating in the water and mud, until I saw the mark of mud on his forehead.

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Anas ibn Sirin related to us. He said: I heard Anas say:

A man of the Ansar said: “I am unable to pray with you.” He was a large man. He prepared food for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and invited him to his house. He spread a mat for him and sprinkled water on the edge of the mat. He prayed two rak‘ahs on it.

A man from the family of al-Jarud said to Anas: “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray Duha?” He said: “I never saw him pray it except on that day.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Hisham, who said: My father related to me. He said: I heard ‘A’ishah relate from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said:

“When supper is set out and the iqamah has been given, begin with supper.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When supper is served, begin with it before you pray the Maghrib prayer, and do not hurry away from your supper.”

‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us, from Abu Usamah, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When supper is set out for one of you and the iqamah has been given, begin with supper, and he should not hurry until he has finished it.”

Food would be set out for Ibn ‘Umar and the iqamah would be given, but he would not go to it until he had finished, while he could hear the imam reciting.

And Zuhayr and Wahb ibn ‘Uthman said: From Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When one of you is eating, he should not hurry until he has satisfied his need for it, even if the iqamah has been given.”

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related it from Wahb ibn ‘Uthman, and Wahb is from Madinah.

‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim related to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Ja‘far ibn ‘Amr ibn Umayyah informed me that his father said:

I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, eating a foreleg, cutting pieces from it. He was called to prayer, so he stood up, put down the knife and prayed without performing ablution.

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Al-Hakam related to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, who said:

I asked ‘A’ishah: “What did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, do in his house?” She said: “He would be occupied in his family’s work”—meaning serving his family—“and when the time for prayer came, he would go out to prayer.”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from Abu Qilabah, who said:

Malik ibn al-Huwayrith came to us in this mosque of ours and said: “I am indeed leading you in prayer, but prayer is not my purpose. I pray as I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray.”

I said to Abu Qilabah: “How did he pray?” He said: “Like this elder of ours.” He said: He was an elderly man who would sit when he raised his head from prostration, before standing up in the first rak‘ah.

Ishaq ibn Nasr related to us. He said: Husayn related to us, from Za’idah, from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr, who said: Abu Burdah related to me, from Abu Musa, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became ill, and his illness grew severe. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: “He is a tender-hearted man. If he stands in your place, he will not be able to lead the people in prayer.” He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” She repeated it, and he said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. You are the women associated with Yusuf.” The messenger came to him, and he led the people in prayer during the lifetime of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, Mother of the Believers, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, that she said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said during his illness: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: I said: “If Abu Bakr stands in your place, he will not make the people hear because of his weeping, so tell ‘Umar to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: I said to Hafsah: “Say to him: ‘If Abu Bakr stands in your place, he will not make the people hear because of his weeping, so tell ‘Umar to lead the people in prayer.’” Hafsah did so. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Stop! You are indeed the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Hafsah said to ‘A’ishah: “I was never to get any good from you.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik al-Ansari informed me—he had followed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, served him and kept his company:

That Abu Bakr used to lead them in prayer during the illness of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in which he died. Then, on Monday, while they were in rows in prayer, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, drew back the curtain of the room and looked towards us while standing. His face was like a page of a copy of the Qur’an. Then he smiled, laughing. We almost became distracted by the joy of seeing the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Abu Bakr stepped backwards to join the row, thinking that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was coming out to prayer. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to us to complete our prayer and let the curtain fall. He died that day.

Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related to us, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not come out for three days. The iqamah was given, and Abu Bakr went forward. The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took hold of the curtain and lifted it. When the face of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, appeared, we had never seen a sight more pleasing to us than the face of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when it appeared to us. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured with his hand to Abu Bakr to go forward. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, let the curtain fall, and he could not be reached until he died.

Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us. He said: Yunus related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Hamzah ibn ‘Abd Allah, that he informed him from his father, who said:

When the pain of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, grew severe, prayer was mentioned to him. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: “Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. When he recites, weeping overcomes him.” He said: “Tell him, and let him pray.” She repeated it to him. He said: “Tell him, and let him pray. You are the women associated with Yusuf.”

Al-Zubaydi, the nephew of al-Zuhri, and Ishaq ibn Yahya al-Kalbi corroborated it from al-Zuhri. And ‘Uqayl and Ma‘mar said: From al-Zuhri, from Hamzah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Zakariyya ibn Yahya related to us. He said: Ibn Numayr related to us. He said: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah informed us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, instructed Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer during his illness, and he used to lead them.

‘Urwah said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt some relief and went out while Abu Bakr was leading the people. When Abu Bakr saw him, he moved back, but he gestured to him to stay as he was. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sat beside Abu Bakr, at his side. Abu Bakr prayed following the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the people prayed following Abu Bakr’s prayer.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu Hazim ibn Dinar, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went to Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf to reconcile them. The time for prayer came, and the caller came to Abu Bakr and said: “Will you lead the people in prayer, so that I may give the iqamah?” He said: “Yes.” Abu Bakr prayed. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came while the people were praying and made his way through until he stood in the row. The people clapped. Abu Bakr did not turn around during his prayer, but when the people clapped repeatedly, he turned and saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to him to stay in his place. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, raised his hands and praised Allah for what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had instructed him to do. Then Abu Bakr moved back until he stood in the row, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went forward and prayed. When he had finished, he said: “Abu Bakr, what prevented you from remaining when I instructed you?” Abu Bakr said: “It was not for Ibn Abi Quhafah to pray in front of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Why did I see you clapping so much? Whoever is troubled by something in his prayer should glorify Allah, for when he glorifies Allah, attention is turned towards him. Clapping is for women.”

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Malik ibn al-Huwayrith, who said:

We came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as young men and stayed with him for about twenty nights. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was merciful. He said: “Why not return to your lands and teach them? Instruct them to pray such-and-such a prayer at such-and-such a time, and such-and-such a prayer at such-and-such a time. When the time for prayer comes, let one of you give the adhan for you, and let the oldest of you lead you.”

Mu‘adh ibn Asad related to us. ‘Abd Allah informed us. Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ informed me. He said: I heard ‘Itban ibn Malik al-Ansari say:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked permission, and I gave him permission. He said: “Where in your house would you like me to pray?” I pointed out the place I liked. He stood, and we formed rows behind him. Then he gave the salutation of peace, and we gave the salutation of peace.

Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us. He said: Za’idah related to us, from Musa ibn Abi ‘A’ishah, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah, who said:

I visited ‘A’ishah and said: “Will you tell me about the illness of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” She said: “Yes. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became seriously ill and said: ‘Have the people prayed?’ We said: ‘No, they are waiting for you.’ He said: ‘Put water for me in the basin.’” She said: “We did so, and he bathed. He tried to rise, but fainted. Then he recovered and said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ‘Have the people prayed?’ We said: ‘No, they are waiting for you, Messenger of Allah.’ He said: ‘Put water for me in the basin.’” She said: “He sat and bathed, then tried to rise, but fainted. Then he recovered and said: ‘Have the people prayed?’ We said: ‘No, they are waiting for you, Messenger of Allah.’ He said: ‘Put water for me in the basin.’ He sat and bathed, then tried to rise, but fainted. Then he recovered and said: ‘Have the people prayed?’ We said: ‘No, they are waiting for you, Messenger of Allah.’ The people remained in the mosque, waiting for the Prophet, peace be upon him, for the later ‘Isha’ prayer.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent to Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. The messenger came to him and said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, instructs you to lead the people in prayer.” Abu Bakr, who was a tender-hearted man, said: “‘Umar, lead the people in prayer.” ‘Umar said to him: “You have more right to do so.” Abu Bakr led the prayers during those days. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt some relief and went out between two men, one of them al-‘Abbas, for the Zuhr prayer. Abu Bakr was leading the people. When Abu Bakr saw him, he began to move back, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to him not to move back. He said: “Seat me beside him.” They seated him beside Abu Bakr. He said: Abu Bakr then prayed following the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the people followed Abu Bakr’s prayer, while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was seated.

‘Ubayd Allah said: I visited ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas and said to him: “Shall I present to you what ‘A’ishah related to me about the illness of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” He said: “Go ahead.” I presented her account to him, and he disputed nothing, except that he said: “Did she name for you the man who was with al-‘Abbas?” I said: “No.” He said: “He was ‘Ali.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, Mother of the Believers, that she said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in his house while ill. He prayed sitting, and people behind him prayed standing. He gestured to them to sit. When he had finished, he said: “The imam is appointed only to be followed. When he bows, bow; when he rises, rise; and when he prays sitting, pray sitting.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rode a horse and was thrown from it, grazing his right side. He performed one of the prayers sitting, and we prayed behind him sitting. When he had finished, he said: “The imam is appointed only to be followed. When he prays standing, pray standing. When he bows, bow; when he rises, rise; and when he says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ say, ‘Our Lord, and to You belongs praise.’ When he prays standing, pray standing; and when he prays sitting, all of you pray sitting.”

Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Al-Humaydi said: His words, “When he prays sitting, pray sitting,” concern his earlier illness. After that, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed sitting while the people behind him were standing, and he did not instruct them to sit. What is taken is the latest, then the latest, of the actions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from Sufyan, who said: Abu Ishaq related to me. He said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yazid related to me. He said: Al-Bara’ related to me—and he was not a liar—who said:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Allah hears whoever praises Him,” none of us bent his back until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had gone down in prostration. Then we went down in prostration after him.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, something similar to this.

Hajjaj ibn Minhal related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad: I heard Abu Hurayrah relate from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Does one of you not fear—or: Does one of you not fear—when he raises his head before the imam, that Allah may turn his head into a donkey’s head, or turn his form into the form of a donkey?”

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Anas ibn ‘Iyad related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said:

When the earliest emigrants came to al-‘Usbah, a place at Quba’, before the arrival of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, used to lead them in prayer. He knew the most Qur’an among them.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. Yahya related to us. Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Abu al-Tayyah related to me, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Listen and obey, even if an Abyssinian whose head is like a raisin is appointed.”

Al-Fadl ibn Sahl related to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Ashyab related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“They lead prayer for you. If they get it right, it is for you; if they get it wrong, it is for you and against them.”

Abu ‘Abd Allah said: And Muhammad ibn Yusuf said to us: Al-Awza‘i related to us. Al-Zuhri related to us, from Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Adi ibn Khiyar:

That he visited ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, while he was under siege. He said: “You are the imam of the community, and what you see has befallen you. An imam involved in turmoil leads us in prayer, and we feel uneasy about it.” He said: “Prayer is the best of what people do. When people do good, do good with them; when they do wrong, avoid their wrongdoing.”

And al-Zubaydi said: Al-Zuhri said: “We do not consider that prayer should be performed behind an effeminate man except out of an unavoidable necessity.”

Muhammad ibn Aban related to us. Ghundar related to us, from Shu‘bah, from Abu al-Tayyah, that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Dharr:

“Listen and obey, even an Abyssinian whose head is like a raisin.”

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard Sa‘id ibn Jubayr relate from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

I spent the night in the house of my maternal aunt Maymunah. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed ‘Isha’, then came and prayed four rak‘ahs, then slept. Then he rose, and I came and stood on his left, so he placed me on his right. He prayed five rak‘ahs, then prayed two rak‘ahs, then slept until I heard his snoring—ghatit, or he said: khatit—then went out to prayer.

Ahmad related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us. He said: ‘Amr related to us, from ‘Abd Rabbih ibn Sa‘id, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, the freedman of Ibn ‘Abbas, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

I slept at Maymunah’s, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was with her that night. He performed ablution, then stood to pray. I stood on his left, and he took me and placed me on his right. He prayed thirteen rak‘ahs, then slept until he breathed audibly. When he slept, he would breathe audibly. Then the caller came to him, and he went out and prayed without performing ablution.

‘Amr said: I related it to Bukayr, and he said: “Kurayb related to me that account.”
