Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim related to us, from Ayyub, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

I spent the night at my maternal aunt’s. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose to pray during the night. I stood to pray with him and stood on his left. He took hold of my head and placed me on his right.

Muslim related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Amr, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah:

That Mu‘adh ibn Jabal used to pray with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then return and lead his people in prayer.

And Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to me. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Amr, who said: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say:

Mu‘adh ibn Jabal used to pray with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then return and lead his people in prayer. He prayed ‘Isha’ and recited al-Baqarah. The man left, and it seemed that Mu‘adh spoke against him. This reached the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: “One who repeatedly causes trial! One who repeatedly causes trial! One who repeatedly causes trial!”—three times—or he said: “One who causes trial! One who causes trial! One who causes trial!” He instructed him to recite two surahs from the middle of the Mufassal.

‘Amr said: “I do not remember them.”

Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us. He said: I heard Qays say: Abu Mas‘ud informed me:

That a man said: “By Allah, Messenger of Allah, I stay away from the morning prayer because of so-and-so, because he makes it so long for us.” I had never seen the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, more angry when giving admonition than he was that day. Then he said: “Some of you drive people away. Whichever of you leads the people in prayer should make it brief, for among them are the weak, the elderly and those with a need.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When one of you leads the people in prayer, he should make it light, for among them are the weak, the sick and the elderly. When one of you prays by himself, he may prolong it as much as he wishes.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. Sufyan related to us, from Isma‘il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Abu Mas‘ud, who said:

A man said: “Messenger of Allah, I stay away from the dawn prayer because so-and-so makes it so long for us.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became angry. I had never seen him more angry in any situation than he was that day. Then he said: “People, some of you drive people away. Whoever leads the people should make it brief, for behind him are the weak, the elderly and those with a need.”

Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Muharib ibn Dithar related to us. He said: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Ansari say:

A man approached with two water-carrying camels when night had fallen. He found Mu‘adh praying, so he left his camel and went towards Mu‘adh. He recited Surat al-Baqarah or al-Nisa’. The man left, and word reached him that Mu‘adh had spoken against him. He went to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and complained to him about Mu‘adh. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Mu‘adh, are you one who repeatedly causes trial—or one who causes trial?”—three times. “Why did you not pray with ‘Glorify the name of your Lord,’ ‘By the sun and its brightness,’ and ‘By the night when it covers’? For behind you pray the elderly, the weak and those with a need.”

I think this is in the hadith.

Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Sa‘id ibn Masruq, Mis‘ar and al-Shaybani followed him in narrating it. ‘Amr, ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Miqsam and Abu al-Zubayr said, from Jabir: Mu‘adh recited al-Baqarah in ‘Isha’. Al-A‘mash followed him in narrating it from Muharib.

Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related to us, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to make the prayer brief and complete it.

Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us. He said: Al-Walid informed us. He said: Al-Awza‘i related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father Abu Qatadah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“I stand in prayer intending to prolong it, then hear a child crying and make my prayer brief, disliking to cause hardship to his mother.”

Bishr ibn Bakr, Ibn al-Mubarak and Baqiyyah followed him in narrating it from al-Awza‘i.

Khalid ibn Makhlad related to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Bilal related to us. He said: Sharik ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say:

I never prayed behind an imam whose prayer was lighter or more complete than that of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He would hear a child crying and make it light, fearing that his mother would be distressed.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ related to us. He said: Sa‘id related to us. He said: Qatadah related to us that Anas ibn Malik related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I begin the prayer intending to prolong it, then hear a child crying and make my prayer brief, knowing the intensity of his mother’s distress at his crying.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ibn Abi ‘Adi related to us, from Sa‘id, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“I begin the prayer and wish to prolong it, then hear a child crying and make it brief, knowing the intensity of his mother’s distress at his crying.”

And Musa said: Aban related to us. Qatadah related to us. Anas related to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the like of it.

Sulayman ibn Harb and Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. They said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir, who said:

Mu‘adh used to pray with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then go to his people and lead them in prayer.

Musaddad related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Dawud related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became ill with the illness in which he died, someone came to inform him of the prayer. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the prayer.” I said: “Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. If he stands in your place, he will weep and be unable to recite.” He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the prayer.” I said the same. On the third or fourth occasion, he said: “You are the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the prayer.” He led the prayer, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out supported between two men. It is as if I can see him tracing the ground with his feet. When Abu Bakr saw him, he began to move back. He gestured to him to pray. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, moved back, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sat beside him, while Abu Bakr made the people hear the takbir.

Muhadir followed him in narrating it from al-A‘mash.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Abu Mu‘awiyah related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became seriously ill, Bilal came to inform him of the prayer. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” I said: “Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. Whenever he stands in your place, he will not make the people hear. If only you would instruct ‘Umar.” He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” I said to Hafsah: “Tell him: ‘Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. Whenever he stands in your place, he will not make the people hear. If only you would instruct ‘Umar.’” He said: “Indeed, you are the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.”

When he began the prayer, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt some relief. He rose, supported between two men, his feet tracing the ground, until he entered the mosque. When Abu Bakr heard his approach, Abu Bakr began to move back. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came until he sat on Abu Bakr’s left. Abu Bakr was praying standing, while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was praying seated. Abu Bakr followed the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the people followed Abu Bakr’s prayer, may Allah Most High be pleased with him.

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik ibn Anas, from Ayyub ibn Abi Tamimah al-Sakhtiyani, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished after two. Dhu al-Yadayn said to him: “Has the prayer been shortened, or have you forgotten, Messenger of Allah?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Has Dhu al-Yadayn spoken the truth?” The people said: “Yes.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood and prayed two more, then gave the salutation of peace. Then he said the takbir and prostrated as he had prostrated, or longer.

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed two rak‘ahs of Zuhr. He was told: “You prayed two rak‘ahs.” He prayed two rak‘ahs, then gave the salutation of peace, then performed two prostrations.

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik ibn Anas related to us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, Mother of the Believers:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said during his illness: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: I said: “If Abu Bakr stands in your place, he will not make the people hear because of his weeping, so tell ‘Umar to lead the prayer.” He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said to Hafsah: “Say to him: ‘If Abu Bakr stands in your place, he will not make the people hear because of his weeping, so tell ‘Umar to lead the people in prayer.’” Hafsah did so. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Stop! Indeed, you are the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Hafsah said to ‘A’ishah: “I was never to get any good from you.”

Abu al-Walid Hisham ibn ‘Abd al-Malik related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Murrah informed me. He said: I heard Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d say: I heard al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“You must straighten your rows, or Allah will certainly make your faces differ.”

Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, from Anas, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Straighten the rows, for I see you behind my back.”

Ahmad ibn Abi Raja’ related to us. He said: Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Amr related to us. He said: Za’idah ibn Qudamah related to us. He said: Humayd al-Tawil related to us. Anas related to us. He said:

The iqamah for prayer was given, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, turned his face towards us and said: “Straighten your rows and stand close together, for I see you from behind my back.”

Abu ‘Asim related to us, from Malik, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The martyrs are: one who drowns, one who dies of plague, one who dies of an abdominal illness, and one who dies under a collapsed structure.” And he said: “If they knew what there is in going early, they would race to it. If they knew what there is in ‘Isha’ and the dawn prayer, they would come to them even crawling. If they knew what there is in the foremost row, they would draw lots.”

‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us. He said: Ma‘mar informed us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said:

“The imam is appointed only to be followed, so do not differ from him. When he bows, bow. When he says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ say, ‘Our Lord, to You belongs praise.’ When he prostrates, prostrate. When he prays sitting, all of you pray sitting. Straighten the row in prayer, for straightening the row is part of the excellence of prayer.”

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Straighten your rows, for straightening the rows is part of establishing the prayer.”

Mu‘adh ibn Asad related to us. He said: Al-Fadl ibn Musa informed me. He said: Sa‘id ibn ‘Ubayd al-Ta’i informed us, from Bashir ibn Yasar al-Ansari, from Anas ibn Malik:

That he came to Madinah and was asked: “What have you disapproved of among us since the time you knew the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” He said: “I have disapproved of nothing except that you do not straighten the rows.”

And ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Ubayd said, from Bashir ibn Yasar: Anas ibn Malik came to us in Madinah—with this account.

‘Amr ibn Khalid related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us, from Humayd, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Straighten your rows, for I see you from behind my back.”

And each of us would place his shoulder against his companion’s shoulder, and his foot against his foot.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Dawud related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Kurayb, the freedman of Ibn ‘Abbas, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

I prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, one night and stood on his left. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took hold of my head from behind me and placed me on his right. He prayed and slept. The caller came to him, and he rose and prayed without performing ablution.

‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Ishaq, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

An orphan and I prayed in our house behind the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and my mother Umm Sulaym was behind us.

Musa related to us. Thabit ibn Yazid related to us. ‘Asim related to us, from al-Sha‘bi, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

One night I stood to pray on the left of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He took me by my hand—or my upper arm—until he placed me on his right, and he reached with his hand from behind me.

Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abdah informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id al-Ansari, from ‘Amrah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray at night in his room. The room’s wall was low, and the people saw the figure of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Some people stood and followed his prayer. In the morning they spoke about that. He stood the second night, and some people stood with him, following his prayer. They did that for two or three nights. After that, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained seated and did not come out. In the morning the people mentioned that. He said: “I feared that the night prayer would be prescribed for you.”

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Fudayk related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had a mat which he spread out by day and used to enclose a space by night. People gathered to him and prayed behind him.

‘Abd al-A‘la ibn Hammad related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah related to us, from Salim Abu al-Nadr, from Busr ibn Sa‘id, from Zayd ibn Thabit:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, made a small room—

He said: “I think he said: of a mat”—

in Ramadan. He prayed in it for several nights, and some of his Companions followed his prayer. When he became aware of them, he began to remain seated. He went out to them and said: “I have understood what I saw you doing. People, pray in your houses, for the best prayer is a person’s prayer in his house, except the prescribed prayer.”

‘Affan said: Wuhayb related to us. Musa related to us: I heard Abu al-Nadr, from Busr, from Zayd, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik al-Ansari informed me:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rode a horse and his right side was grazed. Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said: That day he led us in one of the prayers while seated, and we prayed seated behind him. Then, after he gave the greeting of peace, he said, “The imam has only been appointed to be followed. When he prays standing, pray standing. When he bows, bow; when he rises, rise; and when he prostrates, prostrate. When he says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ say, ‘Our Lord, and to You belongs praise.’”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Layth related to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, fell from a horse and was grazed. He led us in prayer seated, and we prayed seated with him. Then he finished and said, “The imam is only”—or, “The imam has only been appointed”—“to be followed. When he says the takbir, say the takbir; when he bows, bow; and when he rises, rise. When he says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ say, ‘Our Lord, to You belongs praise.’ When he prostrates, prostrate.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us. He said: Abu al-Zinad related to me, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “The imam has only been appointed to be followed. When he says the takbir, say the takbir; when he bows, bow. When he says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ say, ‘Our Lord, and to You belongs praise.’ When he prostrates, prostrate; and when he prays seated, all of you pray seated.”

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn ‘Abdullah, from his father:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to raise his hands level with his shoulders when he began the prayer and when he said the takbir for bowing. When he raised his head from bowing, he also raised them in the same way and said, “Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You belongs praise.” He did not do that in prostration.

Muhammad ibn Muqatil related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri: Salim ibn ‘Abdullah informed me, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raise his hands until they were level with his shoulders when he stood in prayer. He would do that when he said the takbir for bowing, and would do that when he raised his head from bowing, saying, “Allah hears whoever praises Him.” He would not do that in prostration.

Ishaq al-Wasiti related to us. He said: Khalid ibn ‘Abdullah related to us, from Khalid, from Abu Qilabah:

He saw Malik ibn al-Huwayrith, when he prayed, say the takbir and raise his hands. When he intended to bow, he raised his hands; and when he raised his head from bowing, he raised his hands. He related that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did this.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim ibn ‘Abdullah informed us that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said:

I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, begin the takbir in prayer and raise his hands as he said it, until he brought them level with his shoulders. When he said the takbir for bowing, he did the same. When he said, “Allah hears whoever praises Him,” he did the same and said, “Our Lord, and to You belongs praise.” He did not do that when he prostrated or when he raised his head from prostration.

‘Ayyash related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-A‘la related to us. He said: ‘Ubaydullah related to us, from Nafi‘:

When Ibn ‘Umar entered the prayer, he said the takbir and raised his hands. When he bowed, he raised his hands. When he said, “Allah hears whoever praises Him,” he raised his hands. When he stood up after the two rak‘ahs, he raised his hands.

Ibn ‘Umar attributed that to the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Hammad ibn Salamah related it from Ayyub, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Tahman also related it from Ayyub and Musa ibn ‘Uqbah in an abridged form.

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d, who said:

People were instructed that a man should place his right hand on his left forearm during prayer.

Abu Hazim said: I know him only as attributing that to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Isma‘il said, “It is attributed,” and did not say, “He attributes.”

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Do you see my direction of prayer here? By Allah, neither your bowing nor your humility is hidden from me. I certainly see you behind my back.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: I heard Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Perform the bowing and prostration properly. By Allah, I see you behind me”—and sometimes he said, “behind my back”—“when you bow and prostrate.”

Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr and ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, used to begin the prayer with “Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad related to us. He said: ‘Umarah ibn al-Qa‘qa‘ related to us. He said: Abu Zur‘ah related to us. He said: Abu Hurayrah related to us. He said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pause silently between the takbir and the recitation.

He said: I think he said, “briefly.”

I said, “May my father and mother be your ransom, Messenger of Allah. During your silence between the takbir and the recitation, what do you say?” He said, “I say: O Allah, put distance between me and my sins as You have put distance between the east and the west. O Allah, cleanse me of sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt. O Allah, wash away my sins with water, snow and hail.”

Ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Nafi‘ ibn ‘Umar informed us. He said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah related to me, from Asma’ bint Abi Bakr:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed the eclipse prayer. He stood and prolonged the standing, then bowed and prolonged the bowing. Then he stood and prolonged the standing, then bowed and prolonged the bowing. Then he rose, then prostrated and prolonged the prostration. Then he rose, then prostrated and prolonged the prostration. Then he stood and prolonged the standing, then bowed and prolonged the bowing. Then he rose and prolonged the standing, then bowed and prolonged the bowing. Then he rose and prostrated and prolonged the prostration. Then he rose, then prostrated and prolonged the prostration. Then he finished and said: “Paradise came so close to me that, had I ventured towards it, I would have brought you a cluster from its clusters. The Fire came so close to me that I said, ‘O my Lord, am I among them?’ Then there was a woman.”

I think he said:

“A cat was scratching her. I said, ‘What is the matter with this woman?’ They said, ‘She confined it until it died of hunger. She neither fed it nor let it go to eat.’”

Nafi‘ said: I think he said, “From the earth’s khashish, or khashash.”

Musa related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: al-A‘mash related to us, from ‘Umarah ibn ‘Umayr, from Abu Ma‘mar, who said:

We said to Khabbab, “Did the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite in the noon and afternoon prayers?” He said, “Yes.” We said, “How did you recognize that?” He said, “By the movement of his beard.”

Hajjaj related to us. Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Abu Ishaq informed us. He said: I heard ‘Abdullah ibn Yazid delivering a sermon. He said: al-Bara’ related to us, and he was not a liar:

When they prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he raised his head from bowing, they remained standing until they saw that he had prostrated.

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he prayed. They said, “Messenger of Allah, we saw you reach for something in the place where you stood, then we saw you move back.” He said, “I was shown Paradise and reached for a cluster from it. Had I taken it, you would have eaten from it for as long as the world remained.”

Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us. He said: Fulayh related to us. He said: Hilal ibn ‘Ali related to us, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in prayer, then ascended the pulpit and gestured with both hands towards the mosque’s direction of prayer. Then he said, “Just now, since I led you in prayer, I saw Paradise and the Fire represented on the prayer-facing side of this wall. I have never seen the like of today in good and evil”—three times.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id informed us. He said: Ibn Abi ‘Arubah related to us. He said: Qatadah related to us that Anas ibn Malik related to them. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “What is the matter with people who raise their eyes towards the sky during their prayer?” His words about this grew stern until he said, “They must stop doing that, or their eyesight will be snatched away.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu al-Ahwas related to us. He said: Ash‘ath ibn Sulaym related to us, from his father, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

I asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about turning around during prayer. He said, “It is a theft that Satan steals from the servant’s prayer.”

Qutaybah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in a patterned cloak. He said, “Its patterns distracted me. Take it to Abu Jahm and bring me a plain garment.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Layth related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw phlegm on the mosque’s prayer-facing side while he was praying in front of the people, and scraped it away. Then, when he finished, he said, “When one of you is in prayer, Allah is before his face. So no one should spit phlegm in front of his face during prayer.”

Musa ibn ‘Uqbah and Ibn Abi Rawwad related it from Nafi‘.

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Layth ibn Sa‘d related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Anas informed me. He said:

While the Muslims were in the dawn prayer, they were suddenly surprised by the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, lifting the curtain of ‘A’ishah’s room. He looked at them as they stood in rows and smiled with laughter. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, stepped backwards to join the row, thinking that he wanted to come out. The Muslims were on the verge of being distracted from their prayer. He gestured to them, “Complete your prayer.” Then he lowered the curtain, and he died later that day.

Musa related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr related to us, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said:

The people of Kufah complained about Sa‘d to ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, so he removed him and appointed ‘Ammar over them. Their complaints went so far as to say that he did not know how to pray properly. He sent for him and said, “Abu Ishaq, these people claim that you do not know how to pray properly.” Abu Ishaq said, “As for me, by Allah, I used to lead them in the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, without falling short of it. I would pray the night prayer, taking my time in the first two rak‘ahs and making the last two brief.” He said, “That is what we thought of you, Abu Ishaq.” He sent a man—or men—with him to Kufah, and asked the people of Kufah about him. He left no mosque without asking about him, and they spoke well of him, until he entered a mosque of Banu ‘Abs. A man among them called Usamah ibn Qatadah, known as Abu Sa‘dah, stood and said, “Since you have asked us under oath, Sa‘d does not go out with the military expedition, does not divide equally, and does not judge justly.” Sa‘d said, “By Allah, I will pray for three things: O Allah, if this servant of Yours is lying and stood up to show off and seek reputation, prolong his life, prolong his poverty, and expose him to trials.” Afterwards, when he was asked, he would say, “An old man afflicted with trials; Sa‘d’s prayer has struck me.”

‘Abd al-Malik said: I saw him afterwards, when his eyebrows had fallen over his eyes from old age. He would accost young girls in the streets and pinch them.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: al-Zuhri related to us, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘, from ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “There is no prayer for one who does not recite the Opening of the Book.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah, who said: Sa‘id ibn Abi Sa‘id related to me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the mosque. A man entered and prayed, then greeted the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He returned the greeting and said, “Go back and pray, for you have not prayed.” He went back and prayed as he had prayed before. Then he came and greeted the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said, “Go back and pray, for you have not prayed”—three times. He said, “By the One who sent you with the truth, I know no better than this, so teach me.” He said, “When you stand for prayer, say the takbir, then recite whatever is easy for you of the Quran. Then bow until you are at rest while bowing. Then rise until you stand upright. Then prostrate until you are at rest while prostrating. Then rise until you are at rest while sitting. Do that throughout your prayer.”

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: Sa‘d said:

I used to lead them in the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the two afternoon prayers, without falling short of it: I would take my time in the first two rak‘ahs and make the last two brief. ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, “That is what we thought of you.”

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the Opening of the Book and two surahs in the first two rak‘ahs of the noon prayer, making the first longer and the second shorter. Sometimes he would make a verse audible. In the afternoon prayer he would recite the Opening of the Book and two surahs, and would make the first longer. In the dawn prayer he would make the first rak‘ah longer and the second shorter.

‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. He said: My father related to us. He said: al-A‘mash related to us. ‘Umarah related to me, from Abu Ma‘mar, who said:

We asked Khabbab, “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite in the noon and afternoon prayers?” He said, “Yes.” We said, “How did you recognize that?” He said, “By the movement of his beard.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from al-A‘mash, from ‘Umarah ibn ‘Umayr, from Abu Ma‘mar, who said:

I said to Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite in the noon and afternoon prayers?” He said, “Yes.” He said: I said, “How did you know that he was reciting?” He said, “By the movement of his beard.”

Al-Makki ibn Ibrahim related to us, from Hisham, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the Opening of the Book and a surah in each of the two rak‘ahs of the noon and afternoon prayers. Sometimes he would make a verse audible to us.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

Umm al-Fadl heard him reciting “Wa-l-mursalati ‘urfa” and said, “My son, by Allah, your recitation of this surah has reminded me: it was the last one I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite in the sunset prayer.”

Abu ‘Asim related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who said:

Zayd ibn Thabit said to me, “Why do you recite short surahs in the sunset prayer, when I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite the longer of the two long ones?”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut‘im, from his father, who said:

I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite al-Tur in the sunset prayer.

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Mu‘tamir related to us, from his father, from Bakr, from Abu Rafi‘, who said:

I prayed the night prayer with Abu Hurayrah. He recited “Idha al-sama’u inshaqqat” and prostrated. I spoke to him. He said, “I prostrated behind Abu al-Qasim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I will continue to prostrate on reciting it until I meet him.”

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Adi, who said: I heard al-Bara’:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was travelling and recited “al-Tin wa-l-zaytun” in one of the two rak‘ahs of the night prayer.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ related to us. He said: al-Taymi related to me, from Bakr, from Abu Rafi‘, who said:

I prayed the night prayer with Abu Hurayrah. He recited “Idha al-sama’u inshaqqat” and prostrated. I said, “What is this?” He said, “I prostrated on reciting it behind Abu al-Qasim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I will continue to prostrate on reciting it until I meet him.”

Khallad ibn Yahya related to us. He said: Mis‘ar related to us. He said: ‘Adi ibn Thabit related to us that he heard al-Bara’, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, say:

I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite “Wa-l-tini wa-l-zaytun” in the night prayer. I have not heard anyone with a more beautiful voice than his—or recitation.

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu ‘Awn, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Samurah say:

‘Umar said to Sa‘d, “They have complained about you in everything, even the prayer.” He said, “As for me, I prolong the first two rak‘ahs and make the last two brief, and I spare no effort to follow the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” He said, “You have spoken the truth. That is what we thought of you—or what I thought of you.”

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Sayyar ibn Salamah related to us. He said:

My father and I visited Abu Barzah al-Aslami and asked him about the times of the prayers. He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the noon prayer when the sun declined, and the afternoon prayer when a man could return to the furthest part of Madinah while the sun was still bright.

I have forgotten what he said about the sunset prayer.

He did not mind delaying the night prayer until a third of the night. He did not like sleeping before it or conversation afterwards. He would pray the dawn prayer and a man would leave able to recognize the person sitting beside him. He used to recite between sixty and a hundred in the two rak‘ahs—or in one of them.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us. He said: ‘Ata’ informed me that he heard Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, say:

There is recitation in every prayer. What the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, made audible to us, we make audible to you; and what he kept quiet from us, we keep quiet from you. If you recite no more than the Mother of the Quran, it is sufficient; and if you recite more, it is better.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, set out with a group of his companions, heading for the market of ‘Ukaz. The devils had been kept from the news of heaven, and shooting stars had been sent against them. The devils returned to their people, who said, “What is the matter with you?” They said, “We have been kept from the news of heaven, and shooting stars have been sent against us.” They said, “Nothing has come between you and the news of heaven except something that has happened. Travel to the eastern and western parts of the earth, and see what it is that has come between you and the news of heaven.” Those who headed towards Tihamah came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was at Nakhlah, heading for the market of ‘Ukaz, and was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Quran, they listened to it and said, “By Allah, this is what has come between you and the news of heaven.” Then, when they returned to their people, they said, “Our people, ‘We have heard a wondrous Quran, guiding to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.’” Allah then revealed to His Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “Say: It has been revealed to me.”

Only the words of the jinn were revealed to him.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited where he was commanded and remained silent where he was commanded. “Your Lord is never forgetful.” “You have indeed had a good example in the Messenger of Allah.”

‘Ubaydullah said, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

A man of the Ansar used to lead them in prayer in the mosque of Quba’. Whenever he began a surah to recite for them during the prayer, he began with “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” until he finished it, then recited another surah with it. He did this in every rak‘ah. His companions spoke to him, saying, “You begin with this surah, then you do not consider it sufficient until you recite another. Either recite it, or leave it and recite another.” He said, “I will not leave it. If you would like me to lead you in prayer in this way, I will do so; and if you dislike it, I will leave you.” They considered him one of the best of them, and did not want anyone else to lead them. When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to them, they told him what had happened. He said, “So-and-so, what prevents you from doing what your companions ask you to do, and what makes you persist in this surah in every rak‘ah?” He said, “I love it.” He said, “Your love for it has admitted you to the Garden.”

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Abu Wa’il say:

A man came to Ibn Mas‘ud and said, “I recited the Mufassal last night in one rak‘ah.” He said, “Rattling it off like poetry! I know the comparable surahs that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pair together.” He then mentioned twenty surahs of the Mufassal, two surahs in each rak‘ah.

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Hammam related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the Mother of the Book and two surahs in the first two rak‘ahs of the noon prayer, and the Mother of the Book in the last two rak‘ahs. He would make a verse audible to us, and prolong the first rak‘ah more than the second. It was likewise in the afternoon prayer, and likewise in the dawn prayer.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from al-A‘mash, from ‘Umarah ibn ‘Umayr, from Abu Ma‘mar:

I said to Khabbab, “Did the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recite in the noon and afternoon prayers?” He said, “Yes.” We said, “How did you know?” He said, “By the movement of his beard.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. Al-Awza‘i related to us. Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to me. ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah related to me, from his father:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the Mother of the Book and a surah with it in the first two rak‘ahs of the noon and afternoon prayers. Sometimes he would make a verse audible to us. He used to prolong the first rak‘ah.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. Hisham related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to prolong the first rak‘ah of the noon prayer and shorten the second. He would do the same in the dawn prayer.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, who both informed him, from Abu Hurayrah:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “When the imam says Amin, say Amin, for whoever’s saying of Amin coincides with the angels’ saying of Amin will have his previous sins forgiven.”

Ibn Shihab said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say, “Amin.”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “When one of you says Amin and the angels in heaven say Amin, and one coincides with the other, his previous sins are forgiven.”

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Sumayy, the freedman of Abu Bakr, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “When the imam says, ‘Not those upon whom there is anger, nor those who have gone astray,’ say Amin, for whoever’s words coincide with the angels’ words will have his previous sins forgiven.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Amr followed him in relating it, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; and Nu‘aym al-Mujmir, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him.

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Hammam related to us, from al-A‘lam—who is Ziyad—from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah:

He reached the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was bowing, and bowed before he reached the row. He mentioned this to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said, “May Allah increase your eagerness, but do not do it again.”

Ishaq al-Wasiti related to us. He said: Khalid related to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu al-‘Ala’, from Mutarrif, from ‘Imran ibn Husayn, who said:

He prayed with ‘Ali, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, in Basrah, and said, “This man has reminded us of a prayer we used to pray with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” He mentioned that he would say the takbir whenever he rose and whenever he lowered himself.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah:

He used to lead them in prayer, saying the takbir whenever he lowered himself or rose. When he finished, he said, “My prayer resembles the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, more closely than that of any of you.”

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Ghaylan ibn Jarir, from Mutarrif ibn ‘Abdullah, who said:

‘Imran ibn Husayn and I prayed behind ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. When he prostrated, he said the takbir; when he raised his head, he said the takbir; and when he rose after the two rak‘ahs, he said the takbir. When he finished the prayer, ‘Imran ibn Husayn took my hand and said, “This has reminded me of the prayer of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace”—or he said, “He has led us in the prayer of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

‘Amr ibn ‘Awn related to us. He said: Hushaym related to us, from Abu Bishr, from ‘Ikrimah, who said:

I saw a man at the Maqam saying the takbir at every lowering and rising, when he stood and when he lowered himself. I informed Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. He said, “Is that not the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace? May you have no mother!”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Hammam informed us, from Qatadah, from ‘Ikrimah, who said:

I prayed behind an old man in Makkah, and he said the takbir twenty-two times. I said to Ibn ‘Abbas, “He is foolish.” He said, “May your mother be bereaved of you! The practice of Abu al-Qasim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Musa said: Aban related to us. Qatadah related to us. ‘Ikrimah related to us.

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith informed me that he heard Abu Hurayrah say:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood for prayer, he would say the takbir as he stood, then say the takbir as he bowed. Then he would say, “Allah hears whoever praises Him,” as he raised his back from bowing. Then, while standing, he would say, “Our Lord, to You belongs praise.”

‘Abdullah said: “And to You belongs praise.”

Then he would say the takbir as he went down, then say the takbir as he raised his head, then say the takbir as he prostrated, then say the takbir as he raised his head. He would then do this throughout the prayer until he completed it. He would say the takbir when he stood after the two rak‘ahs, after sitting.

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Ya‘fur, who said: I heard Mus‘ab ibn Sa‘d say:

I prayed beside my father, pressed my palms together, then put them between my thighs. My father forbade me and said, “We used to do it, then we were forbidden to do it and commanded to put our hands on our knees.”

Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Sulayman, who said: I heard Zayd ibn Wahb say:

Hudhayfah saw a man who did not complete the bowing and prostration. He said, “You have not prayed. If you were to die, you would die upon something other than the natural disposition with which Allah created Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Badal ibn al-Muhabbar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: al-Hakam informed me, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Bara’, who said:

The bowing of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his prostration, the interval between the two prostrations and when he rose from bowing—apart from the standing and sitting—were approximately equal.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id informed me, from ‘Ubaydullah, who said: Sa‘id al-Maqburi related to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the mosque. A man entered and prayed, then came and greeted the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, returned his greeting and said, “Go back and pray, for you have not prayed.” He prayed, then came and greeted the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said, “Go back and pray, for you have not prayed”—three times. He said, “By Him who sent you with the truth, I do not know how to do otherwise, so teach me.” He said, “When you stand for prayer, say the takbir, then recite what is easy for you of the Quran. Then bow until you are at rest in bowing, then rise until you are upright in standing. Then prostrate until you are at rest in prostration, then rise until you are at rest in sitting, then prostrate until you are at rest in prostration. Then do that throughout your prayer.”

Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say in his bowing and prostration, “Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me.”

Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Allah hears whoever praises Him,” he said, “O Allah, our Lord, and to You belongs praise.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would say the takbir when he bowed and when he raised his head. When he rose from the two prostrations, he said, “Allah is greatest.”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “When the imam says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ say, ‘O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs praise.’ Whoever’s words coincide with the words of the angels will have his previous sins forgiven.”

Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

“I will certainly approximate the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, used to perform qunut in the last rak‘ah of the noon prayer, the night prayer and the dawn prayer, after saying, “Allah hears whoever praises Him.” He would supplicate for the believers and curse the unbelievers.

‘Abdullah ibn Abi al-Aswad related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha’, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

Qunut was in the sunset and dawn prayers.

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Nu‘aym ibn ‘Abdullah al-Mujmir, from ‘Ali ibn Yahya ibn Khallad al-Zuraqi, from his father, from Rifa‘ah ibn Rafi‘ al-Zuraqi, who said:

One day we were praying behind the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When he raised his head from bowing, he said, “Allah hears whoever praises Him.” A man behind him said, “Our Lord, and to You belongs praise—abundant, good, blessed praise.” When he finished, he said, “Who spoke?” He said, “I did.” He said, “I saw thirty-odd angels racing for it, to see which of them would write it first.”

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Thabit, who said:

Anas used to describe for us the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He would pray, and when he raised his head from bowing, he would stand until we would say, “He has forgotten.”

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Bara’, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

The bowing of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his prostration, when he raised his head from bowing and the interval between the two prostrations were approximately equal.

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, who said:

Malik ibn al-Huwayrith used to show us how the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was, and that was outside a prayer time. He stood and settled in the standing position, then bowed and settled in bowing, then raised his head and stood upright for a little while. He led us in a prayer like that of this shaykh of ours, Abu Burayd. When Abu Burayd raised his head from the last prostration, he sat upright, then rose.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb related to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham and Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman informed me:

Abu Hurayrah used to say the takbir in every prayer, obligatory and otherwise, in Ramadan and otherwise. He would say the takbir when he stood, then say the takbir when he bowed, then say, “Allah hears whoever praises Him.” Then he would say, “Our Lord, and to You belongs praise,” before prostrating. Then he would say, “Allah is greatest,” as he went down in prostration, then say the takbir as he raised his head from prostration, then say the takbir as he prostrated, then say the takbir as he raised his head from prostration, then say the takbir as he stood from sitting after the two rak‘ahs. He would do that in every rak‘ah until he finished the prayer. Then, when he finished, he would say, “By Him in whose hand is my soul, my prayer resembles the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, more closely than that of any of you. This was indeed his prayer until he left this world.”

Both of them said: Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, also said:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his head, he would say, “Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You belongs praise.” He would supplicate for men, naming them by their names, saying, “O Allah, rescue al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah and the oppressed among the believers. O Allah, make Your grip severe upon Mudar, and make it years upon them like the years of Yusuf.”

At that time the people of the east, who were from Mudar, were opposing him.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us more than once, from al-Zuhri, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, fell from a horse.

Sometimes Sufyan said, “From a horse.”

His right side was grazed. We went in to visit him. The time for prayer came, and he led us in prayer sitting, and we sat.

On one occasion Sufyan said, “We prayed sitting.”

When he finished the prayer, he said, “The imam has only been appointed to be followed. When he says the takbir, say the takbir; when he bows, bow; when he rises, rise; when he says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ say, ‘Our Lord, and to You belongs praise’; and when he prostrates, prostrate.”

Sufyan said, “Is that how Ma‘mar related it?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “He remembered it well.” That is how al-Zuhri said it: “And to You belongs praise.” I remembered “from his right side.” When we left al-Zuhri, Ibn Jurayj said—and I was with him—“His right leg was grazed.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab and ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid al-Laythi informed me that Abu Hurayrah informed them both:

The people said, “Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?” He said, “Do you doubt the moon on the night of the full moon when there is no veil before it?” They said, “No, Messenger of Allah.” He said, “Do you doubt the sun when there is no cloud before it?” They said, “No.” He said, “You will see Him in that way. The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and He will say, ‘Whoever used to worship something, let him follow it.’ Some of them will follow the sun, some will follow the moon, and some will follow false gods. This community will remain, with its hypocrites among it. Allah will come to them and say, ‘I am your Lord.’ They will say, ‘This is our place until our Lord comes to us. When our Lord comes, we will recognise Him.’ Allah will come to them and say, ‘I am your Lord.’ They will say, ‘You are our Lord.’ He will call them, and the bridge will be set across the midst of Hell. I will be the first of the messengers to cross with his community. No one will speak that day except the messengers, and the words of the messengers that day will be, ‘O Allah, grant safety, grant safety.’

“In Hell there are hooks like the thorns of al-sa‘dan. Have you seen the thorns of al-sa‘dan?” They said, “Yes.” He said, “They are like the thorns of al-sa‘dan, except that no one knows how large they are but Allah. They snatch people according to their deeds. Among them are those ruined by their deeds, and among them are those cut to pieces who then escape. When Allah wishes to have mercy on whomever He wishes among the people of the Fire, Allah commands the angels to bring out those who used to worship Allah. They bring them out and recognise them by the marks of prostration. Allah has forbidden the Fire to consume the mark of prostration. They come out of the Fire. The Fire consumes all of the son of Adam except the mark of prostration. They come out of the Fire charred, and the water of life is poured over them. They grow as a seed grows in the silt carried by a flood.

“Then Allah finishes judging between the servants. A man remains between the Garden and the Fire, and he is the last of the people of the Fire to enter the Garden. His face is turned towards the Fire. He says, ‘My Lord, turn my face away from the Fire. Its smell has poisoned me and its blaze has burned me.’ He says, ‘If that were done for you, might you ask for something else?’ He says, ‘No, by Your might.’ He gives Allah whatever pledge and covenant He wishes, and Allah turns his face away from the Fire. When He turns him towards the Garden, he sees its beauty and remains silent as long as Allah wishes him to remain silent. Then he says, ‘My Lord, bring me near the gate of the Garden.’ Allah says to him, ‘Have you not given pledges and a covenant that you would not ask for anything other than what you had asked for?’ He says, ‘My Lord, may I not be the most wretched of Your creation.’ He says, ‘If you were given that, would you not ask for something else?’ He says, ‘No, by Your might, I will not ask for anything else.’ He gives his Lord whatever pledge and covenant He wishes, and He brings him near the gate of the Garden.

“When he reaches its gate and sees its splendour and the freshness and joy within it, he remains silent as long as Allah wishes him to remain silent. He says, ‘My Lord, admit me to the Garden.’ Allah says, ‘Alas for you, son of Adam! How treacherous you are! Have you not given a pledge and covenant that you would not ask for anything other than what you were given?’ He says, ‘My Lord, do not make me the most wretched of Your creation.’ Allah, mighty and majestic, laughs at him, then permits him to enter the Garden. He says, ‘Wish.’ He wishes until, when his wishes cease, Allah, mighty and majestic, says, ‘Of such and such.’ His Lord begins reminding him, until, when his wishes come to an end, Allah Most High says, ‘You shall have that and the like of it with it.’”

Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri said to Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: Allah said, “You shall have that and ten times its like.” Abu Hurayrah said, “I remember nothing from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, except his saying, ‘You shall have that and the like of it with it.’” Abu Sa‘id said, “I heard him say, ‘You shall have that and ten times its like.’”

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Bakr ibn Mudar related to me, from Ja‘far, from Ibn Hurmuz, from ‘Abdullah ibn Malik ibn Buhaynah:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed, he spread his arms apart until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen.

Al-Layth said: Ja‘far ibn Rabi‘ah related to me something similar.

Al-Salt ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Mahdi related to us, from Wasil, from Abu Wa’il, from Hudhayfah:

He saw a man who did not complete his bowing or his prostration. When he finished his prayer, Hudhayfah said to him, “You have not prayed.”

He said: I think he said, “If you had died, you would have died upon something other than the sunnah of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Qabisah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to prostrate on seven members and not to tuck up hair or clothing: the forehead, the two hands, the two knees and the two feet.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Amr, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

We were commanded to prostrate on seven bones and not to tuck up clothing or hair.

Adam related to us. Isra’il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from ‘Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Khatmi: al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib related to us—and he was not a liar—saying:

We used to pray behind the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When he said, “Allah hears whoever praises Him,” none of us would bend his back until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, placed his forehead on the ground.

Mu‘alla ibn Asad related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

I was commanded to prostrate on seven bones: the forehead (and he pointed with his hand to his nose), the two hands, the two knees and the tips of the feet; and we do not gather up clothing or hair.

Musa related to us. He said: Hammam related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, who said:

I went to Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri and said, “Will you not come out with us to the palm trees so we can talk?” He went out. He said: I said, “Relate to me what you heard from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about the Night of Decree.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, observed retreat during the first ten of Ramadan, and we observed retreat with him. Jibril came to him and said, “What you seek lies ahead of you.” Then he observed retreat during the middle ten, and we observed retreat with him. Jibril came to him and said, “What you seek lies ahead of you.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood to address the people on the morning of the twentieth of Ramadan. He said, “Whoever observed retreat with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, should return. I was shown the Night of Decree, and I forgot it. It is among the last ten, on an odd night. I saw as though I were prostrating in mud and water.” The mosque’s roof was palm branches, and we saw nothing in the sky. Then a cloud came, and rain fell on us. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in prayer until I saw the trace of mud and water on the forehead of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the tip of his nose, confirming his dream.

Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us. He said: Sufyan informed us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d, who said:

People used to pray with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with their waist wrappers tied around their necks because they were small. The women were told, “Do not raise your heads until the men are sitting upright.”

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad—who is Ibn Zayd—related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to prostrate on seven bones and not to gather up his clothing or his hair.

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from ‘Amr, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

I was commanded to prostrate on seven, without gathering up hair or clothing.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Sufyan, who said: Mansur related to me, from Muslim, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, frequently said in his bowing and prostration, “Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me.”

He was putting the Quran into practice.

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah: Malik ibn al-Huwayrith said to his companions:

“Shall I tell you about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” He said: That was not at a time for prayer. He stood, then bowed and said the takbir. Then he raised his head and stood briefly, then prostrated, then raised his head briefly. He prayed the prayer of ‘Amr ibn Salimah, this shaykh of ours.

Ayyub said: He used to do something that I did not see them doing: he used to sit in the third and fourth rak‘ahs.

He said: We came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and stayed with him. He said, “If you would return to your families: pray such-and-such a prayer at such-and-such a time; pray such-and-such a prayer at such-and-such a time. When prayer is due, let one of you give the call to prayer, and let the eldest of you lead you.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahim related to us. He said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah al-Zubayri related to us. He said: Mis‘ar related to us, from al-Hakam, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from al-Bara’, who said:

The prostration of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his bowing and his sitting between the two prostrations were approximately equal in length.

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

I spare no effort to lead you in prayer as I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, lead us in prayer.

Thabit said: Anas used to do something I have not seen you doing. When he raised his head from bowing, he would stand until someone would say, “He has forgotten”; and between the two prostrations, until someone would say, “He has forgotten.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: I heard Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

Be balanced in prostration, and none of you should spread his forearms as a dog spreads them.

Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us. He said: Hushaym informed us. He said: Khalid al-Hadhdha’ informed us, from Abu Qilabah, who said: Malik ibn al-Huwayrith al-Laythi informed us:

He saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying. When he was in an odd-numbered rak‘ah of his prayer, he did not rise until he was sitting upright.

Mu‘alla ibn Asad related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, who said:

Malik ibn al-Huwayrith came to us and led us in prayer in this mosque of ours. He said, “I am leading you in prayer, but I do not intend the prayer; I want to show you how I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray.”

Ayyub said: I asked Abu Qilabah, “What was his prayer like?” He said, “Like the prayer of this shaykh of ours,” meaning ‘Amr ibn Salimah. Ayyub said: That shaykh used to complete the takbir. When he raised his head from the second prostration, he sat, supported himself on the ground, then stood.

Yahya ibn Salih related to us. He said: Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us, from Sa‘id ibn al-Harith, who said:

Abu Sa‘id led us in prayer. He said the takbir aloud when he raised his head from prostration, when he prostrated, when he rose and when he stood after the two rak‘ahs. He said, “This is how I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us. He said: Ghaylan ibn Jarir related to us, from Mutarrif, who said:

‘Imran and I prayed a prayer behind ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. When he prostrated, he said the takbir; when he rose, he said the takbir; and when he stood after the two rak‘ahs, he said the takbir. When he said the closing greeting, ‘Imran took my hand and said, “This man has led us in the prayer of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace”; or he said, “This has reminded me of the prayer of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from ‘Abdullah, who informed him:

He used to see ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, sitting cross-legged when he sat in prayer. I did so, being young at the time. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar forbade me and said, “The practice of prayer is to set your right foot upright and bend the left.” I said, “But you do that.” He said, “My legs do not support me.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Khalid, from Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Halhalah, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn ‘Ata’.

And al-Layth related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib and Yazid ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn Halhalah, from Muhammad ibn ‘Amr ibn ‘Ata’:

He was sitting with a group of the companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. We mentioned the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Abu Humayd al-Sa‘idi said, “I remembered the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, better than any of you. I saw that when he said the takbir, he put his hands level with his shoulders. When he bowed, he placed his hands firmly on his knees, then bent his back. When he raised his head, he stood upright until every vertebra returned to its place. When he prostrated, he placed his hands down, neither spreading them out flat nor drawing them in close, and pointed the tips of his toes towards the qiblah. When he sat after the two rak‘ahs, he sat on his left foot and set the right upright. When he sat in the last rak‘ah, he brought his left foot forward, set the other upright and sat on his buttocks.”

Al-Layth heard Yazid ibn Abi Habib; Yazid heard Muhammad ibn Halhalah; and Ibn Halhalah heard Ibn ‘Ata’. Abu Salih said, from al-Layth: “Every vertebra.” Ibn al-Mubarak said, from Yahya ibn Ayyub, who said: Yazid ibn Abi Habib related to me that Muhammad ibn ‘Amr related to him: “Every vertebra.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz related to me—a client of Banu ‘Abd al-Muttalib (on one occasion he said: a client of Rabi‘ah ibn al-Harith)—from ‘Abdullah ibn Buhaynah, who was from Azd Shanu’ah, was an ally of Banu ‘Abd Manaf and was one of the companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led them in the noon prayer. He stood after the first two rak‘ahs without sitting, and the people stood with him. When he had completed the prayer and the people awaited his closing greeting, he said the takbir while sitting, then made two prostrations before saying the closing greeting. Then he said the closing greeting.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Bakr related to us, from Ja‘far ibn Rabi‘ah, from al-A‘raj, from ‘Abdullah ibn Malik ibn Buhaynah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in the noon prayer. He stood when he should have sat. At the end of his prayer, he made two prostrations while sitting.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us, from Shaqiq ibn Salamah, who said: ‘Abdullah said:

When we prayed behind the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, we used to say, “Peace be upon Jibril and Mika’il. Peace be upon so-and-so and so-and-so.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, turned to us and said, “Allah is Peace. When one of you prays, let him say: ‘Greetings belong to Allah, and prayers and good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and Allah’s mercy and blessings. Peace be upon us and upon Allah’s righteous servants.’ When you say this, it reaches every righteous servant of Allah in heaven and earth. ‘I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.’”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed us, from ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who informed him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate in prayer: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of the false messiah, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of life and the trial of death. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from sin and debt.” Someone said to him, “How often you seek refuge from debt!” He said, “When a man falls into debt, he speaks and lies, and he promises and breaks his promise.”

And from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah informed me that ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, seek refuge in his prayer from the trial of the Dajjal.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

He said to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “Teach me a supplication to make in my prayer.” He said, “Say: ‘O Allah, I have greatly wronged myself, and no one forgives sins but You. So forgive me with forgiveness from You, and have mercy on me. You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.’”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from al-A‘mash: Shaqiq related to me, from ‘Abdullah, who said:

When we were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in prayer, we used to say, “Peace be upon Allah from His servants. Peace be upon so-and-so and so-and-so.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Do not say, ‘Peace be upon Allah,’ for Allah is Peace. Instead say: ‘Greetings belong to Allah, and prayers and good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and Allah’s mercy and blessings. Peace be upon us and upon Allah’s righteous servants.’ When you say this, it reaches every servant in heaven or between heaven and earth. ‘I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger.’ Then he chooses whichever supplication he likes best and supplicates.”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, who said: I asked Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, and he said:

I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prostrating in water and mud, until I saw the trace of mud on his forehead.

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us. Al-Zuhri related to us, from Hind bint al-Harith: Umm Salamah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, said:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said the closing greeting, the women would rise as soon as he finished saying it. He remained a little while before rising.

Ibn Shihab said: I think—and Allah knows best—that he remained so the women could leave before those of the people who departed caught up with them.

Hibban ibn Musa related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘, from ‘Itban, who said:

We prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said the closing greeting when he said it.

‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ informed me. He stated that he remembered the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and remembered a mouthful of water that he spat out from a bucket that was in their house. He said: I heard ‘Itban ibn Malik al-Ansari, one of Banu Salim, say:

I used to lead my people, Banu Salim, in prayer. I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “I have noticed my eyesight failing, and the floods come between me and my people’s mosque. I would like you to come and pray in a place in my house so I can take it as a place of prayer.” He said, “I will do so, if Allah wills.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to me in the morning, with Abu Bakr accompanying him, after the day had grown intense. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked permission to enter, and I gave him permission. He did not sit down before saying, “Where in your house would you like me to pray?” He pointed out to him the place where he wanted him to pray. He stood, and we formed rows behind him. Then he said the closing greeting, and we said it when he said it.

Ishaq ibn Nasr related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us. He said: ‘Amr informed me that Abu Ma‘bad, a client of Ibn ‘Abbas, informed him that Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, informed him:
