Raising the voice in remembrance when people departed from the obligatory prayer took place in the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Ibn ‘Abbas said: I used to know when they had departed by hearing it.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: ‘Amr related to us. He said: Abu Ma‘bad informed me, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

I used to recognise the completion of the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, by the takbir.

Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr related to us. He said: Mu‘tamir related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

The poor came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “Those with abundant wealth have taken the high ranks and lasting bliss. They pray as we pray and fast as we fast, but they have surplus wealth with which they perform Hajj and ‘Umrah, strive in jihad and give charity.” He said, “Shall I tell you of something which, if you take it up, will let you catch up with those who preceded you, and no one after you will catch up with you, and you will be the best of those among whom you live, except someone who does the same? You glorify Allah, praise Him and declare His greatness after every prayer, thirty-three times.”

We disagreed among ourselves. Some of us said, “We glorify thirty-three times, praise thirty-three times and declare His greatness thirty-four times.” I went back to him, and he said, “You say, ‘Glory be to Allah,’ ‘Praise belongs to Allah,’ and ‘Allah is greatest,’ until all of them are thirty-three.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr, from Warrad, the secretary of al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah, who said:

Al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah dictated to me in a letter to Mu‘awiyah that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say after every obligatory prayer: “There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion, and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. O Allah, none can withhold what You give, and none can give what You withhold, and wealth does not benefit the wealthy person against You.”

Shu‘bah said, from ‘Abd al-Malik, with this report; from al-Hakam, from al-Qasim ibn Mukhaymirah, from Warrad, with this report. Al-Hasan said: Jadd means wealth.

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Jarir ibn Hazim related to us. He said: Abu Raja’ related to us, from Samurah ibn Jundub, who said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had prayed a prayer, he turned his face towards us.

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Mas‘ud, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in the dawn prayer at al-Hudaybiyah after rain during the night. When he finished, he turned towards the people and said, “Do you know what your Lord said?” They said, “Allah and His messenger know best.” He said, “Among My servants this morning are a believer in Me and a disbeliever. As for whoever said, ‘We were given rain by Allah’s favour and mercy,’ that person believes in Me and disbelieves in the star. But whoever said, ‘By the naw’ of such-and-such a star,’ that person disbelieves in Me and believes in the star.”

‘Abdullah related to us; he heard Yazid, who said: Humayd informed us, from Anas, who said:

One night the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed the prayer until half the night had passed. Then he came out to us. When he had prayed, he turned his face towards us and said, “The people have prayed and gone to sleep, but you will remain in prayer as long as you wait for the prayer.”

Abu al-Walid related to us. Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us. Al-Zuhri related to us, from Hind bint al-Harith, from Umm Salamah:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said the closing greeting, he would remain in his place a little while.

Ibn Shihab said: We think—and Allah knows best—that this was so those of the women who were leaving could depart.

Ibn Abi Maryam said: Nafi‘ ibn Yazid informed us. He said: Ja‘far ibn Rabi‘ah informed me that Ibn Shihab wrote to him, saying: Hind bint al-Harith al-Firasiyyah related to me, from Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and she was one of her companions—who said:

He would say the closing greeting, and the women would leave and enter their homes before the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, departed.

Ibn Wahb said, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab: Hind al-Firasiyyah informed me. ‘Uthman ibn ‘Umar said: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri: Hind al-Firasiyyah related to me. Al-Zubaydi said: Al-Zuhri informed me that Hind bint al-Harith al-Qurashiyyah informed him. She was married to Ma‘bad ibn al-Miqdad, who was an ally of Banu Zuhrah, and she used to visit the wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Shu‘ayb said, from al-Zuhri: Hind al-Qurashiyyah related to me. Ibn Abi ‘Atiq said, from al-Zuhri, from Hind al-Firasiyyah. Al-Layth said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to me; he related to him from Ibn Shihab, from a woman of Quraysh who related to him from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Muhammad ibn ‘Ubayd related to us. He said: ‘Isa ibn Yunus related to us, from ‘Umar ibn Sa‘id, who said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me, from ‘Uqbah, who said:

I prayed the afternoon prayer behind the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in Madinah. He said the closing greeting, then rose quickly and stepped over the people’s necks towards one of his wives’ rooms. The people were startled by his haste. He came out to them and saw that they were surprised by his haste, so he said, “I remembered some uncoined gold we had. I disliked its holding me back, so I ordered it to be distributed.”

Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Sulayman, from ‘Umarah ibn ‘Umayr, from al-Aswad, who said: ‘Abdullah said:

None of you should give Satan a share of his prayer by thinking that he is obliged to depart only to his right. I have often seen the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, depart to his left.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah, who said: Nafi‘ related to me, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said during the expedition of Khaybar:

Whoever eats from this plant—meaning garlic—must not approach our mosque.

‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Abu ‘Asim related to us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us. He said: ‘Ata’ informed me. He said: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

Whoever eats from this plant—he means garlic—must not come to us in our mosques.

I asked, “What does he mean by it?” He said, “I only think he means it raw.” Makhlad ibn Yazid said, from Ibn Jurayj: “Only its foul smell.”

Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab: ‘Ata’ stated that Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah stated that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever eats garlic or onions should keep away from us”; or he said, “Should keep away from our mosque and stay in his house.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought a pot containing green vegetables. He noticed a smell from them, asked about it and was told what vegetables it contained. He said, “Bring it near,” to one of his companions who was with him. When he saw it, he disliked eating it. He said, “Eat, for I converse privately with those with whom you do not converse.”

Ahmad ibn Salih said, from Ibn Wahb: He was brought a badr. Ibn Wahb said: Meaning a platter containing greens. Al-Layth and Abu Safwan did not mention the story of the pot from Yunus. I do not know whether it is a statement of al-Zuhri or part of the hadith. Ahmad ibn Salih said, after Yunus’s report from Ibn Shihab: He confirms Yunus’s statement.

Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, who said:

A man asked Anas, “What did you hear Allah’s Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mention about garlic?” He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Whoever eats from this plant must not come near us, or must not pray with us.”

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Ghundar related to me. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: I heard Sulayman al-Shaybani say: I heard al-Sha‘bi say:

Someone who passed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, by an isolated grave informed me that he led them in prayer and they formed rows at it.

I said, “Abu ‘Amr, who related this to you?” He said, “Ibn ‘Abbas.”

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Safwan ibn Sulaym related to me, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

Bathing on Friday is obligatory for everyone who has reached puberty.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan informed us, from ‘Amr, who said: Kurayb informed me, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

One night I stayed with my maternal aunt Maymunah, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, slept. When part of the night had passed, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, got up and performed a light ablution from a hanging worn waterskin.

‘Amr described it as light and very small in amount.

Then he stood to pray. I got up and performed ablution much as he had, then came and stood on his left. He moved me and placed me on his right. Then he prayed as much as Allah willed, then lay down and slept until he snored. The caller came and informed him of the prayer. He got up with him to go to the prayer, prayed, and did not perform ablution.

We said to ‘Amr, “Some people say that the eye of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sleeps, but his heart does not sleep.” ‘Amr said, “I heard ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Umayr say: ‘The dreams of the prophets are revelation.’” Then he recited: {I see in a dream that I am slaughtering you.}

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik:

His grandmother Mulaykah invited the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to some food she had prepared. He ate some of it and said, “Get up so I may lead you in prayer.” I went to a mat of ours that had become black from long use and sprinkled it with water. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood. The orphan was with me and the old woman behind us. He led us in two rak‘ahs.

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

I approached riding a she-donkey. At that time I had nearly reached puberty, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was leading the people in prayer at Mina without a wall in front of him. I passed in front of part of the row, dismounted, let the she-donkey graze and entered the row. No one objected to what I had done.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘A’ishah said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed until late.

‘Ayyash said: ‘Abd al-A‘la related to us. Ma‘mar related to us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed the night prayer until ‘Umar called to him, “The women and children have gone to sleep.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out and said, “No one among the people of the earth is praying this prayer except you.”

At that time no one prayed except the people of Madinah.

‘Amr ibn ‘Ali related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abis related to me: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both.

A man said to him, “Were you present when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out?” He said, “Yes. Had it not been for my position with him, I would not have been present”—meaning because of his youth. He came to the marker by the house of Kathir ibn al-Salt, then gave an address. Then he came to the women, admonished them, reminded them and instructed them to give charity. A woman would reach with her hand to her throat, dropping something into Bilal’s garment. Then he and Bilal came to the house.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed the night prayer until ‘Umar called to him, “The women and children have gone to sleep.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out and said, “No one among the people of the earth is waiting for it except you.”

At that time prayer was performed only in Madinah. They used to pray the night prayer between the disappearance of twilight and the first third of the night.

‘Ubaydullah ibn Musa related to us, from Hanzalah, from Salim ibn ‘Abdullah, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

When your women ask your permission at night to go to the mosque, give them permission.

Shu‘bah corroborated it, from al-A‘mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. ‘Uthman ibn ‘Umar related to us. Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Hind bint al-Harith related to me that Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, informed her:

In the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the women would rise when they had said the closing greeting of the obligatory prayer. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the men who had prayed remained as long as Allah willed. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose, the men rose.

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik.

And ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Amrah bint ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would indeed pray the dawn prayer, and the women would leave wrapped in their garments, unrecognisable in the darkness.

Muhammad ibn Miskin related to us. He said: Bishr related to us. Al-Awza‘i informed us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to me, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah al-Ansari, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

I stand to pray intending to make it long, but I hear a child crying and shorten my prayer, disliking to cause hardship to his mother.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Amrah, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

Had the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, seen what the women had introduced, he would have prevented them, as the women of the Children of Israel were prevented.

I asked ‘Amrah, “Were they prevented?” She said, “Yes.”

Yahya ibn Qaza‘ah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Hind bint al-Harith, from Umm Salamah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said the closing greeting, the women would rise as soon as he finished saying it. He would remain in his place a little while before rising.

He said: We think—and Allah knows best—that this was so the women could leave before any of the men caught up with them.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah related to us, from Ishaq, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in the house of Umm Sulaym. An orphan and I stood behind him, and Umm Sulaym stood behind us.

Yahya ibn Musa related to us. Sa‘id ibn Mansur related to us. Fulayh related to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the dawn prayer in the darkness. The women of the believers would leave, unrecognisable because of the darkness, or they would not recognise one another.

Musaddad related to us. Yazid ibn Zuray‘ related to us, from Ma‘mar, from al-Zuhri, from Salim ibn ‘Abdullah, from his father, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

If the wife of any of you asks permission, he must not prevent her.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah related to us, from Ishaq, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in the house of Umm Sulaym. An orphan and I stood behind him, and Umm Sulaym stood behind us.

Yahya ibn Qaza‘ah related to us. Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Hind bint al-Harith, from Umm Salamah, who said:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said the closing greeting, the women would rise as soon as he finished saying it. He would remain in his place a little while before rising.

She said: We think—and Allah knows best—that this was so the women could leave before the men caught up with them.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us. He said: Abu al-Zinad related to us that ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz al-A‘raj, the freedman of Rabi‘ah ibn al-Harith, related to him that he heard Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

He heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say, “We are the last, but the foremost on the Day of Resurrection, although they were given the Book before us. Then this was their day which was made obligatory for them, but they differed over it, so Allah guided us. The people follow us in this: the Jews tomorrow and the Christians the day after tomorrow.”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “When one of you comes to the Friday prayer, let him take a bath.”

‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma’ related to us. He said: Juwayriyah informed us, from Malik, from al-Zuhri, from Salim ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

While ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab was standing delivering the sermon on Friday, a man from the earliest Emigrants among the Companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered. ‘Umar called out to him, “What time is this?” He said, “I was occupied and did not return to my family until I heard the call to prayer. I did no more than perform ablution.” He said, “And only ablution as well! You know that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to command bathing.”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Bathing on Friday is obligatory for every male who has reached puberty.”

‘Ali related to us. He said: Harami ibn ‘Umarah related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Bakr ibn al-Munkadir, who said: ‘Amr ibn Sulaym al-Ansari related to me:

He said: I testify that Abu Sa‘id said: I testify that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Bathing on Friday is obligatory for every male who has reached puberty, and cleaning the teeth with a toothstick, and applying perfume if it is available.”

‘Amr said: As for bathing, I testify that it is obligatory. As for cleaning the teeth and perfume, Allah knows best whether it is obligatory or not, but this is how it appears in the hadith.

Abu ‘Abdullah said: He is the brother of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir. This Abu Bakr’s personal name was not given. Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, Sa‘id ibn Abi Hilal and several others narrated this from him. Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir was known by the kunyahs Abu Bakr and Abu ‘Abdullah.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Sumayy, the freedman of Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Whoever bathes on Friday with the bath for major ritual impurity and then goes, it is as though he has offered a camel. Whoever goes in the second hour, it is as though he has offered a cow. Whoever goes in the third hour, it is as though he has offered a horned ram. Whoever goes in the fourth hour, it is as though he has offered a hen. Whoever goes in the fifth hour, it is as though he has offered an egg. When the imam comes out, the angels attend to listen to the remembrance.”

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah:

While ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, was delivering the sermon on Friday, a man entered. ‘Umar said, “Why do you delay coming to prayer?” The man said, “It was only that when I heard the call, I performed ablution.” He said, “Did you not hear the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say, ‘When one of you goes to the Friday prayer, let him take a bath’?”

Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, who said: My father informed me, from Ibn Wadi‘ah, from Salman al-Farisi:

He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “No man bathes on Friday, purifies himself as much as he can, applies some of his oil or some perfume from his household, then goes out without separating two people, then prays what has been allotted to him, then listens silently when the imam speaks, without being forgiven for what lies between that Friday and the other Friday.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri:

Tawus said: I said to Ibn ‘Abbas, “They mentioned that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Bathe on Friday, wash your heads even if you are not in a state of major ritual impurity, and apply perfume.’” Ibn ‘Abbas said, “As for bathing, yes; as for perfume, I do not know.”

Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us. He said: Hisham informed us that Ibn Jurayj informed them. He said: Ibrahim ibn Maysarah informed me, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

He mentioned the Prophet’s words, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about bathing on Friday. I said to Ibn ‘Abbas, “Does he apply perfume or oil if it is available in his household?” He said, “I do not know of it.”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar:

‘Umar ibn al-Khattab saw a silk robe at the door of the mosque. He said, “Messenger of Allah, if only you bought this and wore it on Friday and for delegations when they come to you.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Only someone who has no share in the Hereafter wears this.” Then robes of this kind came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he gave ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, one of them. ‘Umar said, “Messenger of Allah, you have clothed me with it, yet you said what you said about ‘Utarid’s robe.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “I did not clothe you with it for you to wear it.” So ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, gave it to a brother of his in Makkah who was a polytheist.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Were it not that I would cause hardship to my community—or to the people—I would have commanded them to use the toothstick with every prayer.”

Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb ibn al-Habhab related to us. Anas related to us:

He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “I have spoken to you often about the toothstick.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us. He said: Sufyan informed us, from Mansur and Husayn, from Abu Wa’il, from Hudhayfah:

He said: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose during the night, he would clean his mouth.

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Bilal related to me. He said: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah said: My father informed me, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

She said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr entered with a toothstick which he was using. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, looked at it. I said to him, “Give me this toothstick, ‘Abd al-Rahman.” He gave it to me, and I broke it, then chewed it, then gave it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He used it while leaning against my chest.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim, from ‘Abd al-Rahman—he is Ibn Hurmuz—from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite in the dawn prayer on Friday: {Alif. Lam. Mim. The revelation} and {Has there come upon man}.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Abu ‘Amir al-‘Aqadi related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Tahman related to us, from Abu Jamrah al-Duba‘i, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

He said: The first Friday prayer held after the Friday prayer in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was in the mosque of ‘Abd al-Qays at Juwathi in al-Bahrayn.

Bishr ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim ibn ‘Abdullah informed us, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Each of you is a shepherd.”

Al-Layth added: Yunus said: Ruzayq ibn Hukaym wrote to Ibn Shihab, while I was with him that day in Wadi al-Qura, “Do you think I should hold the Friday prayer?” Ruzayq was in charge of land which he cultivated, and on it was a group of Black people and others. Ruzayq was then in charge of Aylah. Ibn Shihab wrote, while I was listening, commanding him to hold the Friday prayer and informing him that Salim had related to him that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

“Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock. The imam is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock. A man is a shepherd in his household, and he is responsible for his flock. A woman is a shepherd in her husband’s house and is responsible for her flock. A servant is a shepherd over his master’s property and is responsible for his flock.”

He said: I think he also said:

“A man is a shepherd over his father’s property and is responsible for his flock. Each of you is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim ibn ‘Abdullah related to me that he heard ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say, “Whoever among you comes to the Friday prayer, let him take a bath.”

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Bathing on Friday is obligatory for every male who has reached puberty.”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: Ibn Tawus related to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah:

He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “We are the last, but the foremost on the Day of Resurrection. They were given the Book before us, and we were given it after them. This is the day over which they differed, and Allah guided us. Tomorrow is for the Jews and the day after tomorrow for the Christians.”

He fell silent, then said:

“It is a duty upon every Muslim to bathe on one day in every seven, washing his head and his body.”

Aban ibn Salih narrated it from Mujahid, from Tawus, from Abu Hurayrah:

He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Allah Most High has a right upon every Muslim that he bathe on one day in every seven.”

‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. Shababah related to us. Warqa’ related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Umar:

From the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said, “Permit women to go to the mosques at night.”

Yusuf ibn Musa related to us. Abu Usamah related to us. ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Umar related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar:

He said: A wife of ‘Umar used to attend the dawn and night prayers in congregation in the mosque. She was asked, “Why do you go out when you know that ‘Umar dislikes that and is jealous?” She said, “What prevents him from forbidding me?” He said, “What prevents him is the saying of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ‘Do not prevent Allah’s female servants from Allah’s mosques.’”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Hamid, the companion of al-Ziyadi, informed me. He said: ‘Abdullah ibn al-Harith, the cousin of Muhammad ibn Sirin, related to us:

Ibn ‘Abbas said to his caller to prayer on a rainy day, “When you say, ‘I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,’ do not say, ‘Come to prayer.’ Say, ‘Pray in your homes.’” It was as though the people disapproved. He said, “Someone better than me did this. Friday prayer is an obligation, but I disliked putting you in difficulty, so that you would walk through mud and slippery ground.”

Ahmad related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah ibn Wahb related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Abi Ja‘far, that Muhammad ibn Ja‘far ibn al-Zubayr related to him, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

She said: People used to come on Friday from their homes and from al-‘Awali. They would come through the dust; dust and sweat would affect them, and sweat would come out of them. One of them came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was with me. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “If only you would purify yourselves for this day of yours.”

‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id informed us that he asked ‘Amrah about bathing on Friday:

She said: ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, said: People used to do their own work. When they went to the Friday prayer, they went in their working condition. They were told, “If only you would bathe.”

Surayj ibn al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us, from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Uthman al-Taymi, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the Friday prayer when the sun began to decline.

‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Humayd informed us, from Anas:

He said: We used to hold the Friday prayer early and take our midday rest after the Friday prayer.

Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami related to us. He said: Harami ibn ‘Umarah related to us. He said: Abu Khaldah—he is Khalid ibn Dinar—related to us. He said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say:

When it was very cold, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would pray early, and when it was very hot, he would delay the prayer until it was cooler.

Meaning the Friday prayer.

Yunus ibn Bukayr said: Abu Khaldah informed us, and he said “the prayer” without mentioning the Friday prayer.

Bishr ibn Thabit said: Abu Khaldah related to us:

He said: An emir led us in the Friday prayer, then said to Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, “How did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray the noon prayer?”

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: ‘Abayah ibn Rifa‘ah related to us:

He said: Abu ‘Abs caught up with me while I was going to the Friday prayer. He said, “I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say, ‘Whoever’s feet become dusty in the path of Allah, Allah forbids him to the Fire.’”

Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us. Al-Zuhri said, from Sa‘id and Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

And Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah:

Said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say, “When the prayer is established, do not come to it running. Come to it walking, keeping calm. Pray what you catch, and complete what you miss.”

‘Amr ibn ‘Ali related to us. He said: Abu Qutaybah related to me. He said: ‘Ali ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah:

I know it only as being from his father.

From the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said, “Do not stand up until you see me, and remain calm.”

‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b informed us, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from his father, from Ibn Wadi‘ah, from Salman al-Farisi:

He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Whoever bathes on Friday and purifies himself as much as he can, then applies oil or some perfume, then goes without separating two people, prays what has been allotted to him, and then listens silently when the imam comes out, is forgiven for what lies between it and the other Friday.”

Muhammad related to us. He said: Makhlad ibn Yazid informed us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us. He said: I heard Nafi‘ say: I heard Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade a man from making his brother get up from his seat and sitting in it.

I said to Nafi‘, “Friday prayer?” He said, “Friday prayer and others.”

Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from al-Zuhri, from al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid:

He said: Originally, the call on Friday was made when the imam sat on the pulpit, during the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr and ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both. When it was ‘Uthman’s time, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, and the people had increased in number, he added the third call at al-Zawra’.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Abi Salamah al-Majishun related to us, from al-Zuhri, from al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid:

The one who added the third call to prayer on Friday was ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, when the people of Madinah increased in number. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had only one caller to prayer. The call to prayer on Friday was made when the imam sat down.

Meaning on the pulpit.

Ibn Muqatil related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Abu Bakr ibn ‘Uthman ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf informed us, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf:

He said: I heard Mu‘awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan while he was sitting on the pulpit. The caller to prayer gave the call and said, “Allah is greater. Allah is greater.” Mu‘awiyah said, “Allah is greater. Allah is greater.” He said, “I testify that there is no god but Allah.” Mu‘awiyah said, “And I.” He said, “I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.” Mu‘awiyah said, “And I.” When the call was finished, he said, “People, I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in this very place, when the caller gave the call, saying what you have heard me say.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, that al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid informed him:

The second call to prayer on Friday was ordered by ‘Uthman when the people of the mosque increased in number. The call to prayer on Friday was made when the imam sat down.

Muhammad ibn Muqatil related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: I heard al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid:

He said: Originally, the call to prayer on Friday was made when the imam sat on the pulpit on Friday, during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr and ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both. During the caliphate of ‘Uthman, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, when they had increased in number, ‘Uthman ordered the third call to prayer on Friday. It was given at al-Zawra’, and the practice remained that way.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Ya‘qub ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abd, al-Qari al-Qurashi al-Iskandarani related to us. He said: Abu Hazim ibn Dinar related to us:

Some men came to Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi, having disagreed about what wood the pulpit was made of. They asked him about it. He said, “By Allah, I certainly know what it is made of. I saw it on the first day it was put in place and the first day the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sat on it. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent to a certain woman, whom Sahl named: ‘Instruct your slave, the carpenter, to make me pieces of wood on which I can sit when I speak to the people.’ She instructed him, and he made them from tamarisk from al-Ghabah. Then he brought them, and she sent them to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He ordered them to be put here. Then I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray on them and say the takbir while on them, then bow while on them. Then he descended backwards and prostrated at the foot of the pulpit, then returned. When he finished, he turned to the people and said, ‘People, I only did this so that you would follow me and learn my prayer.’”

Sa‘id ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id informed me. He said: Ibn Anas informed me that he heard Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah:

He said: There was a trunk by which the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to stand. When the pulpit was put in place for him, we heard from the trunk sounds like those of she-camels in late pregnancy, until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came down and placed his hand on it.

Sulayman said, from Yahya: Hafs ibn ‘Ubaydullah ibn Anas informed me that he heard Jabir.

Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father:

He said: I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delivering a sermon on the pulpit. He said, “Whoever comes to the Friday prayer, let him take a bath.”

‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Umar al-Qawariri related to us. He said: Khalid ibn al-Harith related to us. He said: ‘Ubaydullah related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to deliver the sermon standing, then sit down, then stand up, as you do now.

Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Hilal ibn Abi Maymunah. ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar related to us that he heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri:

He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sat on the pulpit one day, and we sat around him.

And Mahmud said: Abu Usamah related to us. He said: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah related to us. He said: Fatimah bint al-Mundhir informed me, from Asma’ bint Abi Bakr:

She said: I went in to ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, while the people were praying. I said, ‘What is happening with the people?’ She pointed her head towards the sky. I said, ‘A sign?’ She nodded her head, meaning yes. She said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prolonged it greatly, until faintness overcame me. Beside me was a waterskin containing water, so I opened it and began pouring from it over my head. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished, and the sun had cleared. He addressed the people and praised Allah as He deserves, then said, ‘Now then.’ And she said: Some women of the Ansar made a noise, so I turned towards them to quiet them. I said to ‘A’ishah, ‘What did he say?’ She said: He said, ‘There is nothing that I had not been shown before that I have not seen at this place where I stand, even the Garden and the Fire. It has been revealed to me that you will be tried in the graves with a trial like, or close to, the trial of the false messiah. One of you will be approached and asked, “What do you know of this man?” As for the believer—or he said, the one who is certain; Hisham was unsure—he will say, “He is the Messenger of Allah. He is Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He brought us clear proofs and guidance, so we believed, responded, followed and affirmed the truth.” He will be told, “Sleep, righteous one. We already knew that you did indeed believe in him.” As for the hypocrite—or he said, the doubter; Hisham was unsure—he will be asked, “What do you know of this man?” He will say, “I do not know. I heard people saying something, so I said it.”’

Hisham said: Fatimah did indeed tell it to me, and I retained it, except that she mentioned what would be made severe for him.

Muhammad ibn Ma‘mar related to us. He said: Abu ‘Asim related to us, from Jarir ibn Hazim. He said: I heard al-Hasan saying: ‘Amr ibn Taghlib related to us:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought wealth or captives. He divided it, giving to some men and leaving others. News reached him that those he had left were displeased. He praised Allah, then extolled Him, then said, ‘Now then. By Allah, I give to one man and leave another, although the one I leave is more beloved to me than the one I give to. But I give to some people because of the distress and anxiety I see in their hearts, and I entrust others to the contentment and goodness that Allah has placed in their hearts. Among them is ‘Amr ibn Taghlib.’ By Allah, I would not wish to have red camels in exchange for those words of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Yunus corroborated this.

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab. He said: ‘Urwah informed me that ‘A’ishah informed him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out one night in the middle of the night and prayed in the mosque. Some men prayed following his prayer. In the morning, the people spoke about it, and more of them gathered and prayed with him. In the morning, the people spoke about it, and the number of people in the mosque increased on the third night. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out, and they prayed following his prayer. On the fourth night, the mosque could not hold its people, until he came out for the dawn prayer. When he had finished the dawn prayer, he faced the people and pronounced the testimony of faith, then said, ‘Now then. Your presence was not hidden from me, but I feared that it would be made obligatory upon you and you would be unable to perform it.’

Yunus corroborated this.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. He said: ‘Urwah informed me, from Abu Humayd al-Sa‘idi, who informed him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up one evening after the prayer, pronounced the testimony of faith and extolled Allah as He deserves, then said, ‘Now then.’

Abu Mu‘awiyah and Abu Usamah corroborated this, from Hisham, from his father, from Abu Humayd, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said, ‘Now then.’

Al-‘Adani corroborated this, from Sufyan, concerning ‘Now then.’

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. He said: ‘Ali ibn Husayn related to me, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah:

He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up, and I heard him saying, when he pronounced the testimony of faith, ‘Now then.’

Al-Zubaydi corroborated this, from al-Zuhri.

Isma‘il ibn Aban related to us. He said: Ibn al-Ghasil related to us. He said: ‘Ikrimah related to us, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ascended the pulpit. It was the last gathering in which he sat. He had wrapped a cloak around his shoulders and tied a dark headcloth around his head. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said, ‘People, come to me.’ They gathered towards him. Then he said, ‘Now then. This community of the Ansar will become fewer, while the people become more numerous. Whoever takes charge of any part of the community of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and is able in that position to harm someone or benefit someone, should accept from those among them who do good and pardon those among them who do wrong.’

Musaddad related to us. He said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us. He said: ‘Ubaydullah related to us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abdullah:

He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to deliver two sermons, sitting between them.

Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu ‘Abdullah al-Agharr, from Abu Hurayrah:

He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘When Friday comes, the angels stand at the door of the mosque, recording the first to arrive, then the next. The likeness of the one who comes early is that of someone offering a camel, then someone offering a cow, then a ram, then a hen, then an egg. When the imam comes out, they fold up their sheets and listen to the remembrance.’

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah:

He said: A man came while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was addressing the people on Friday. He said, ‘Have you prayed, so-and-so?’ He said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘Stand up and pray two units of prayer.’

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Amr, who heard Jabir:

He said: A man entered on Friday while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon. He said, ‘Have you prayed?’ He said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘Stand up and pray two units of prayer.’

Musaddad related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, from Anas; and from Yunus, from Thabit, from Anas:

He said: While the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon on Friday, a man stood up and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, the horses have perished and the sheep have perished. Ask Allah to give us rain.’ He extended his hands and supplicated.

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Al-Walid related to us. He said: Abu ‘Amr related to us. He said: Ishaq ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah related to me, from Anas ibn Malik:

He said: The people suffered a drought in the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. While the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon one Friday, a Bedouin stood up and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, the livestock have perished and the dependants are hungry. Supplicate to Allah for us.’ He raised his hands, and we could see no patch of cloud in the sky. By Him in whose hand is my soul, he had not lowered them before clouds rose like mountains. Then he had not come down from his pulpit before I saw rain streaming down his beard, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Rain fell upon us that day, the next day, the day after it and the day following, until the next Friday. That Bedouin—or he said, someone else—stood up and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, the buildings have collapsed and the livestock have drowned. Supplicate to Allah for us.’ He raised his hands and said, ‘Allah, around us and not upon us.’ Whenever he pointed his hand towards a part of the clouds, they parted. Madinah became like an opening, and the valley of Qanat flowed for a month. No one came from any direction without speaking of the abundant rain.

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab. He said: Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab informed me that Abu Hurayrah informed him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘If you say to your companion on Friday, “Listen quietly,” while the imam is delivering the sermon, you have engaged in idle speech.’

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioned Friday and said, ‘In it is a time that no Muslim servant meets while standing in prayer, asking Allah Most High for something, without Him giving it to him.’ He indicated with his hand how short it was.

Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Amr related to us. He said: Za’idah related to us, from Husayn, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d. He said: Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah related to us:

He said: While we were praying with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, a caravan carrying food arrived. They turned towards it until only twelve men remained with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Then this verse was revealed: ‘When they see trade or diversion, they disperse towards it and leave you standing.’

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray two units before the noon prayer and two units after it, two units after the sunset prayer in his house, and two units after the night prayer. He would not pray after Friday prayer until he had departed, then he would pray two units.

Sa‘id ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Abu Ghassan related to us. He said: Abu Hazim related to me, from Sahl:

He said: There was a woman among us who planted chard along irrigation channels in a field of hers. When Friday came, she would pull up the chard roots and put them in a pot. Then she would add a handful of barley that she ground, so the chard roots served as its meat. We would leave Friday prayer and greet her. She would bring that food near to us, and we would lick it up. We used to long for Friday because of that food of hers.

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Hazim related to us, from his father, from Sahl:

With this account, and he said: We would neither take our midday rest nor eat lunch until after Friday prayer.

Muhammad ibn ‘Uqbah al-Shaybani related to us. He said: Abu Ishaq al-Fazari related to us, from Humayd:

He said: I heard Anas saying: We used to go early to Friday prayer, then take our midday rest.

Sa‘id ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Abu Ghassan related to us. He said: Abu Hazim related to me, from Sahl:

He said: We used to pray the Friday prayer with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and afterwards would come the midday rest.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri.

He said: I asked him, ‘Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray?’—meaning the fear prayer. He said: Salim informed me that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said:

I went on an expedition with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, towards Najd. We faced the enemy and formed ranks opposite them. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood to lead us in prayer. One group stood with him, praying, while another group faced the enemy. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bowed with those who were with him and made two prostrations. Then they went to take the place of the group that had not prayed. That group came, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed one unit with them and made two prostrations. Then he gave the closing greeting. Each of them then stood and prayed one unit for himself and made two prostrations.

Sa‘id ibn Yahya ibn Sa‘id al-Qurashi related to us. He said: My father related to me. He said: Ibn Jurayj related to us, from Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar:

Something similar to Mujahid’s statement: When they become intermingled, they pray standing. Ibn ‘Umar added, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ‘If they are more numerous than that, let them pray standing or mounted.’

Haywah ibn Shurayh related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Harb related to us, from al-Zubaydi, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood, and the people stood with him. He said ‘Allah is greatest,’ and they said it with him. He bowed, and some of the people bowed. Then he prostrated, and they prostrated with him. Then he stood for the second unit. Those who had prostrated stood and guarded their brothers. The other group came and bowed and prostrated with him. All the people were in prayer, but they were guarding one another.

Yahya related to us. He said: Waki‘ related to us, from ‘Ali ibn Mubarak, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah. He said:

‘Umar came on the day of the Ditch and began cursing the unbelievers of Quraysh, saying, ‘Messenger of Allah, I had not prayed ‘Asr until the sun was almost setting.’ The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘And by Allah, I have not prayed it yet either.’ He said: He went down to Buthan, performed ablution and prayed ‘Asr after the sun had set. Then he prayed Maghrib after it.

‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma’ related to us. He said: Juwayriyah related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar. He said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, returned from al-Ahzab, he said to us, ‘Let no one pray ‘Asr except at Banu Qurayzah.’ The time for ‘Asr reached some of them on the way. Some said, ‘We will not pray until we reach it.’ Others said, ‘Rather, we will pray; that was not intended of us.’ This was mentioned to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he did not rebuke any of them.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb and Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed the dawn prayer while it was still dark. Then he mounted and said, ‘Allah is greatest! Khaybar is ruined. When we descend into a people’s open space, evil is the morning of those who have been warned.’ They came out running in the streets, saying, ‘Muhammad and al-khamis!’ He said: Al-khamis means the army. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, overcame them, killed the fighting men and took the children captive. Safiyyah came to Dihyah al-Kalbi, and then to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He then married her and made her freedom her bridal gift.

‘Abd al-‘Aziz said to Thabit, ‘Abu Muhammad, did you ask Anas what he gave her as a bridal gift?’ He said, ‘He gave her herself as her bridal gift.’ Then he smiled.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. He said: Salim ibn ‘Abdullah informed me that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said:

‘Umar took a robe of thick silk that was being sold in the market. He took it and came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, buy this and adorn yourself with it for Eid and for delegations.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, ‘This is only the clothing of one who has no share.’ ‘Umar remained as long as Allah willed him to remain. Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent him a robe of silk brocade. ‘Umar came with it and brought it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said, ‘Messenger of Allah, you said, “This is only the clothing of one who has no share,” yet you have sent me this robe.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, ‘Sell it, or meet your need with it.’

Ahmad related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us. He said: ‘Amr informed us that Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Asadi related to him, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah. She said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to me while two girls were with me, singing the songs of Bu‘ath. He lay down on the bed and turned his face away. Abu Bakr came in and rebuked me, saying, ‘A pipe of Satan in the presence of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace!’ The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, turned towards him and said, ‘Leave them both.’ When he became inattentive, I signalled to the two of them, and they went out.

It was an Eid day, and the Black people were playing with shields and spears. Either I asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, or he said, ‘Would you like to watch?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He stood me behind him, my cheek against his cheek, while he was saying, ‘Carry on, Banu Arfidah!’ When I grew tired, he said, ‘Is that enough for you?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Then go.’

Hajjaj related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Zubayd informed me. He said: I heard al-Sha‘bi, from al-Bara’. He said:

I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delivering a sermon. He said, ‘The first thing we begin with on this day of ours is to pray, then return and sacrifice. Whoever does that has followed our practice.’

‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her. She said:

Abu Bakr came in while two girls from among the girls of the Ansar were with me, singing what the Ansar had said to one another on the day of Bu‘ath.

She said: They were not singers.

Abu Bakr said, ‘Pipes of Satan in the house of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?’ It was an Eid day. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Abu Bakr, every people has an Eid, and this is our Eid.’

Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahim related to us. Sa‘id ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Hushaym related to us. He said: ‘Ubaydullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Anas informed us, from Anas. He said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would not go out in the morning on the day of Fitr until he had eaten some dates.

Murajja’ ibn Raja’ said: ‘Ubaydullah related to me. He said: Anas related to me, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: He would eat them in an odd number.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Anas. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Whoever slaughtered before the prayer must do it again.’ A man stood and said, ‘This is a day on which meat is desired,’ and he mentioned some of his neighbours. It was as though the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, accepted his statement. He said, ‘I have a young she-goat dearer to me than two sheep for meat.’ The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, allowed it for him.

I do not know whether the permission extended to anyone other than him or not.

‘Uthman related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from al-Sha‘bi, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, addressed us on the day of Adha after the prayer. He said, ‘Whoever prays our prayer and performs our sacrifice has fulfilled the sacrifice. Whoever sacrifices before the prayer has done so before the prayer, and has no sacrifice.’ Abu Burdah ibn Niyar, al-Bara’s maternal uncle, said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I sacrificed my sheep before the prayer. I knew that today was a day of eating and drinking, and I wanted my sheep to be the first thing slaughtered in my house. So I slaughtered my sheep and ate my midday meal before coming to the prayer.’ He said, ‘Your sheep is a sheep for meat.’ He said, ‘Messenger of Allah, we have a young she-goat that is dearer to me than two sheep. Will it suffice for me?’ He said, ‘Yes, but it will not suffice for anyone after you.’

Sa‘id ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far related to us. He said: Zayd informed me, from ‘Iyad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Sarh, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri. He said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would go out on the day of Fitr and Adha to the prayer ground. The first thing he began with was the prayer. Then he would turn and stand facing the people, while they remained seated in their rows. He would admonish them, counsel them and give them instructions. If he wished to dispatch a force, he dispatched it, or to order something, he ordered it. Then he would leave.

Abu Sa‘id said: The people continued in this way until I went out with Marwan, who was the governor of Madinah, on Adha or Fitr. When we reached the prayer ground, there was a pulpit built by Kathir ibn al-Salt. Marwan wanted to climb it before praying. I pulled at his garment, and he pulled me. He went up and delivered the sermon before the prayer. I said to him, ‘By Allah, you have changed things.’ He said, ‘Abu Sa‘id, what you know has gone.’ I said, ‘By Allah, what I know is better than what I do not know.’ He said, ‘The people would not remain seated for us after the prayer, so I placed it before the prayer.’

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Anas related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would pray at Adha and Fitr, then deliver the sermon after the prayer.

Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us. He said: Hisham informed us that Ibn Jurayj informed them. He said: ‘Ata’ informed me, from Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah. He said: I heard him say:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out on the day of Fitr and began with the prayer before the sermon.

He said: ‘Ata’ also informed me:

Ibn ‘Abbas sent word to Ibn al-Zubayr when allegiance was first pledged to him: No call was made for the prayer on the day of Fitr; the sermon was only after the prayer.

‘Ata’ also informed me, from Ibn ‘Abbas and from Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah. They both said:

No call was made on the day of Fitr or on the day of Adha.

And from Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah. He said: I heard him say:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood and began with the prayer, then addressed the people afterwards. When the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had finished, he came down and went to the women and reminded them, leaning on Bilal’s hand. Bilal was spreading out his garment, into which the women were putting charity.

I said to ‘Ata’, ‘Do you consider it a duty for the imam now to go to the women and remind them when he has finished?’ He said, ‘That is indeed a duty upon them. Why should they not do it?’

Abu ‘Asim related to us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Muslim informed me, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas. He said:

I attended Eid with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, ‘Umar and ‘Uthman, may Allah Most High be pleased with them. All of them would pray before the sermon.

Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us. He said: ‘Ubaydullah related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar. He said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr and ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, would pray the two Eids before the sermon.

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Adi ibn Thabit, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed two rak‘ahs on the day of Fitr. He did not pray before it or after it. Then he went to the women, with Bilal beside him, and commanded them to give charity. They began throwing things in: a woman would throw in her earring and her necklace.

Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Zubayd related to us. He said: I heard al-Sha‘bi, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘The first thing we begin with on this day of ours is to pray, then return and sacrifice. Whoever does that has followed our practice. Whoever sacrifices before the prayer has merely presented meat to his family; it is no part of the sacrifice.’ A man of the Ansar called Abu Burdah ibn Niyar said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I have slaughtered, and I have a young she-goat better than a mature animal.’ He said, ‘Put it in its place, but it will not fulfil—or suffice—for anyone after you.’

Zakariyya ibn Yahya, Abu al-Sukayn, related to us. He said: Al-Muharibi related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Suqah related to us, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr. He said:

I was with Ibn ‘Umar when the point of a spear struck the arch of his foot, and his foot stuck to the stirrup. I dismounted and pulled it free. This was at Mina. News reached al-Hajjaj, and he began visiting him. Al-Hajjaj said, ‘If we knew who injured you!’ Ibn ‘Umar said, ‘You injured me.’ He said, ‘How?’ He said, ‘You carried weapons on a day when they were not carried, and you brought weapons into the Sanctuary when weapons were not brought into the Sanctuary.’

Ahmad ibn Ya‘qub related to us. He said: Ishaq ibn Sa‘id ibn ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id ibn al-‘As related to me, from his father:

He said: Al-Hajjaj entered upon Ibn ‘Umar while I was with him. He said, ‘How is he?’ He said, ‘Well.’ He said, ‘Who injured you?’ He said, ‘The one who ordered weapons to be carried on a day when carrying them is not lawful injured me.’

Meaning al-Hajjaj.

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Zubayd, from al-Sha‘bi, from al-Bara’. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, addressed us on the Day of Sacrifice. He said, ‘The first thing we begin with on this day of ours is to pray, then return and sacrifice. Whoever does that has followed our practice. Whoever slaughters before praying has merely hastened meat for his family; it is no part of the sacrifice.’ My maternal uncle, Abu Burdah ibn Niyar, stood and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I slaughtered before praying, and I have a young she-goat better than a mature animal.’ He said, ‘Put it in its place’—or he said, ‘Slaughter it’—‘and a young she-goat will not suffice for anyone after you.’

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Malik ibn Anas related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Thaqafi related to me. He said:

I asked Anas about the talbiyah while the two of us were going in the morning from Mina to ‘Arafat: ‘What did you use to do with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?’ He said, ‘The one saying the talbiyah would say it without being objected to, and the one saying the takbir would say it without being objected to.’

Muhammad related to us. ‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. He said: My father related to us, from ‘Asim, from Hafsah, from Umm ‘Atiyyah. She said:

We used to be commanded to go out on the day of Eid, even bringing the virgin girl out of her secluded room, and even bringing out the menstruating women. They would be behind the people, saying the takbir with their takbir and supplicating with their supplication, hoping for the blessing of that day and its purification.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: ‘Ubaydullah related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar:

A spear would be planted in front of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Fitr and Sacrifice, then he would pray.

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Al-Walid related to us. He said: Abu ‘Amr related to us. He said: Nafi‘ informed me, from Ibn ‘Umar. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would go in the morning to the prayer ground. A short spear would be carried before him and set up in front of him at the prayer ground, and he would pray facing it.

‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Umm ‘Atiyyah. She said:

We were commanded to bring out the young women and the women in seclusion.

And from Ayyub, from Hafsah, similarly.

He added in Hafsah’s report—he said, or she said:

‘The young women and the women in seclusion; and the menstruating women should keep apart from the prayer ground.’

‘Amr ibn ‘Abbas related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman related to us. Sufyan related to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman. He said: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas. He said:

I went out with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a day of Fitr or Adha. He prayed, then delivered a sermon, then went to the women, admonished them, reminded them and commanded them to give charity.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Talhah related to us, from Zubayd, from al-Sha‘bi, from al-Bara’. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to al-Baqi‘ on the day of Adha and prayed two rak‘ahs. Then he turned his face towards us and said, ‘The first of our rites on this day of ours is to begin with prayer, then return and sacrifice. Whoever does that has followed our practice. Whoever slaughters before that has merely hastened something for his family; it is no part of the sacrifice.’ A man stood and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I have slaughtered, and I have a young she-goat better than a mature animal.’ He said, ‘Slaughter it, but it will not suffice for anyone after you.’

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Sufyan. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abis related to me. He said: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas:

He was asked, ‘Did you attend Eid with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?’ He said, ‘Yes. Had it not been for my young age, I would not have attended it. He reached the marker by the house of Kathir ibn al-Salt, prayed, then delivered a sermon. Then he went to the women with Bilal. He admonished them, reminded them and commanded them to give charity. I saw them reaching with their hands and throwing it into Bilal’s garment. Then he and Bilal went to his house.’

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Nasr related to me. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us. He said: Ibn Jurayj related to us. He said: ‘Ata’ informed me, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah. He said: I heard him say:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood on the day of Fitr and prayed. He began with prayer, then delivered a sermon. When he finished, he came down and went to the women and reminded them, leaning on Bilal’s hand. Bilal had spread out his garment, into which the women were throwing charity.

I said to ‘Ata’, ‘The zakat of the day of Fitr?’ He said, ‘No, but charity they were giving at that time. A woman would throw in her large rings, and they would throw things in.’ I said, ‘Do you consider that a duty upon the imam—to go to them and remind them?’ He said, ‘It is certainly a duty upon them. Why do they not do it?’

Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Hasan ibn Muslim also informed me, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both. He said:

I attended Fitr with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, ‘Umar and ‘Uthman, may Allah Most High be pleased with them. They would pray it before the sermon, then he would deliver the sermon afterwards. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out. It is as though I am looking at him as he motions with his hand for people to sit. Then he went forward, making his way through them, until he came to the women with Bilal. He said, ‘O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you’—the verse. When he finished it, he said, ‘Are you committed to that?’ One woman among them said, ‘Yes’; no one else answered him.

Hasan did not know who she was.

He said, ‘Then give charity.’ Bilal spread out his garment, then said, ‘Come, may my father and mother be ransomed for you.’ They began throwing large rings and rings into Bilal’s garment.

‘Abd al-Razzaq said: The fatakh were the large rings that were used in the time of ignorance.

Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from Hafsah bint Sirin. She said:

We used to prevent our girls from going out on the day of Eid. A woman came and stayed at the palace of Banu Khalaf. I went to her, and she related that her sister’s husband had gone on twelve expeditions with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and her sister was with him on six expeditions. She said, ‘We used to tend the sick and treat the wounded.’ She said, ‘Messenger of Allah, is there any blame on one of us if she has no outer garment and does not go out?’ He said, ‘Let her companion cover her with her outer garment, and let them witness the good and the supplication of the believers.’ Hafsah said: When Umm ‘Atiyyah arrived, I went to her and asked her, ‘Did you hear about such-and-such?’ She said, ‘Yes, may my father be ransomed for him.’

She seldom mentioned the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, without saying, ‘May my father be ransomed for him.’

He said, ‘Let the young women in seclusion go out’—or he said, ‘The young women and the women in seclusion’—

Ayyub was uncertain.

‘And the menstruating women. Let the menstruating women keep apart from the prayer ground, and let them witness the good and the supplication of the believers.’ She said: I said to her, ‘The menstruating women?’ She said, ‘Yes. Does not a menstruating woman attend ‘Arafat, and attend such-and-such, and attend such-and-such?’

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Ibn Abi ‘Adi related to us, from Ibn ‘Awn, from Muhammad. He said: Umm ‘Atiyyah said:

We were commanded to go out, so we would bring out the menstruating women, the young women and the women in seclusion.

Ibn ‘Awn said: Or the young women in seclusion.

As for the menstruating women, they would witness the gathering of the Muslims and their supplication, but keep apart from their prayer ground.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us. He said: Kathir ibn Farqad related to me, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would sacrifice or slaughter at the prayer ground.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu al-Ahwas related to us. He said: Mansur ibn al-Mu‘tamir related to us, from al-Sha‘bi, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib. He said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, addressed us on the Day of Sacrifice after the prayer. He said, ‘Whoever prays our prayer and performs our sacrifice has fulfilled the sacrifice. Whoever sacrifices before the prayer, that is a sheep for meat.’ Abu Burdah ibn Niyar stood and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I sacrificed before going out to the prayer. I knew that today was a day of eating and drinking, so I made haste, ate and fed my family and my neighbours.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘That is a sheep for meat.’ He said, ‘I have a young she-goat that is better than two sheep for meat. Will it suffice for me?’ He said, ‘Yes, but it will not suffice for anyone after you.’

Hamid ibn ‘Umar related to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, that Anas ibn Malik said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed on the Day of Sacrifice, then delivered a sermon. He commanded whoever had slaughtered before the prayer to repeat his slaughter. A man of the Ansar stood and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I have neighbours’—either he said, ‘They are in need,’ or he said, ‘In poverty’—‘and I slaughtered before the prayer. I have a young she-goat dearer to me than two sheep for meat.’ He allowed it for him.

Muslim related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Aswad, from Jundab. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed on the Day of Sacrifice, then delivered a sermon, then slaughtered. He said, ‘Whoever slaughtered before praying must slaughter another in its place. Whoever has not slaughtered must slaughter in the name of Allah.’

Muhammad related to us. He said: Abu Tumaylah, Yahya ibn Wadih, informed us, from Fulayh ibn Sulayman, from Sa‘id ibn al-Harith, from Jabir. He said:

When it was a day of Eid, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would take a different route.

Yunus ibn Muhammad corroborated him, from Fulayh, from Sa‘id, from Abu Hurayrah. Jabir’s report is sounder.

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah:

Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, came in to her. There were two girls with her during the days of Mina, playing the duff and beating it, while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was covered with his garment. Abu Bakr rebuked them, so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, uncovered his face and said, ‘Leave them, Abu Bakr, for these are days of Eid.’

Those days were the days of Mina.

‘A’ishah said: I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, screening me while I watched the Abyssinians playing in the mosque. ‘Umar rebuked them, so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Leave them. You are safe, Banu Arfidah.’

Meaning, in the sense of safety.
