Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: ‘Adi ibn Thabit related to me. He said: I heard Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out on the day of Fitr and prayed two rak‘ahs. He did not pray before it or after it, and Bilal was with him.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘ and ‘Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn ‘Umar:

A man asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about the night prayer. The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said, “The night prayer is two units at a time. If one of you fears the coming of morning, he prays one unit, making what he has prayed odd in number.”

And from Nafi‘:

‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar used to give the closing greeting between the single unit and the two units of Witr, even giving instructions about some need of his.

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, that Ibn ‘Abbas informed him:

He spent the night with Maymunah, who was his maternal aunt. I lay across the width of a pillow, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his wife lay along its length. He slept until midnight, or close to it. Then he awoke, wiping sleep from his face, and recited ten verses from Al ‘Imran. Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went to an old waterskin that was hanging and performed ablution well. Then he stood to pray. I did as he had done and stood beside him. He placed his right hand on my head and took hold of my ear, twisting it. Then he prayed two units, then two units, then two units, then two units, then two units, then two units. Then he prayed Witr. Then he lay down until the caller to prayer came to him. He got up and prayed two units, then went out and prayed the morning prayer.

Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to me. He said: ‘Amr informed me that ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim related to him, from his father, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “The night prayer is two units at a time. When you wish to finish, pray one unit, making what you have prayed odd in number.”

Al-Qasim said: Since we reached maturity, we have seen people praying Witr with three units. There is latitude in either way. I hope there is nothing wrong with any of it.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, that ‘A’ishah informed him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray eleven units. That was his prayer.

She means at night.

In that prayer, he would remain in a prostration for as long as it takes one of you to recite fifty verses before raising his head. He would pray two units before the dawn prayer, then lie on his right side until the caller to prayer came to him for the prayer.

Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us. He said: Anas ibn Sirin related to us. He said:

I said to Ibn ‘Umar, “Tell me about the two units before the morning prayer: should I prolong the recitation in them?” He said, “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray at night two units at a time and pray Witr with one unit. He would pray the two units before the morning prayer as though the call to prayer were in his ears.”

Hammad said: Meaning, quickly.

‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. He said: My father related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: Muslim related to me, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah. She said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed Witr at every part of the night, and his Witr eventually came to be at the time before dawn.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: My father related to me, from ‘A’ishah. She said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray while I lay asleep across his bed. When he wanted to pray Witr, he would wake me, and I would pray Witr.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah: Nafi‘ related to me, from ‘Abdullah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said:

“Make Witr your last prayer at night.”

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Abu Bakr ibn ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, from Sa‘id ibn Yasar, that he said:

I was travelling with ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar on the road to Makkah. Sa‘id said: When I feared the coming of morning, I dismounted and prayed Witr, then caught up with him. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said, “Where were you?” I said, “I feared the coming of morning, so I dismounted and prayed Witr.” ‘Abdullah said, “Do you not have a good example in the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” I said, “Yes, by Allah.” He said, “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray Witr on the camel.”

Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Juwayriyah ibn Asma’ related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar. He said:

When travelling, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the night prayer on his mount, making gestures, whichever way it turned with him, except for the obligatory prayers. He would pray Witr on his mount.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad. He said:

Anas was asked, “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform qunut in the morning prayer?” He said, “Yes.” He was asked, “Did he perform qunut before bowing?” He said, “After bowing, for a short time.”

Ahmad ibn Yunus informed us. He said: Za’idah related to us, from al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz, from Anas. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed qunut for a month, supplicating against Ri‘l and Dhakwan.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Khalid related to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas. He said:

Qunut was performed in the sunset and dawn prayers.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from ‘Abbad ibn Tamim, from his uncle, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to seek rain and turned his cloak.

Qutaybah related to us. Mughirah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman related to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his head in the last unit of prayer, he would say, “O Allah, rescue ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah. O Allah, rescue Salamah ibn Hisham. O Allah, rescue al-Walid ibn al-Walid. O Allah, rescue the oppressed believers. O Allah, intensify Your pressure upon Mudar. O Allah, make it years like the years of Yusuf.” And the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Ghifar—may Allah forgive it; and Aslam—may Allah grant it peace.”

Ibn Abi al-Zinad said, from his father: All of this was in the morning prayer.

‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said:

We were with ‘Abdullah, and he said: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw the people turning away, he said, “O Allah, seven like the seven of Yusuf.” A year of scarcity overtook them and consumed everything, until they ate hides, carrion and decaying carcasses. One of them would look at the sky and see smoke from hunger. Abu Sufyan came to him and said, “O Muhammad, you command obedience to Allah and maintaining ties of kinship. Your people have perished, so supplicate to Allah for them.” Allah Most High said, “So watch for the day when the sky brings clear smoke,” up to His words, “returning—the day We strike the greatest blow.” The blow was on the day of Badr. The smoke, the blow, al-lizam and the sign of the Romans have already passed.

‘Amr ibn ‘Ali related to us. He said: Abu Qutaybah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Dinar related to us, from his father, who said:

I heard Ibn ‘Umar reciting Abu Talib’s poetry:

And a fair one, through whose face rain is sought from the clouds,

a refuge for orphans, a protection for widows.

And ‘Umar ibn Hamzah said: Salim related to us, from his father:

At times I remembered the poet’s words while looking at the face of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as he sought rain. He would not come down until every waterspout gushed:

And a fair one, through whose face rain is sought from the clouds,

a refuge for orphans, a protection for widows.

And these are Abu Talib’s words.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah al-Ansari related to us. He said: My father, ‘Abdullah ibn al-Muthanna, related to me, from Thumamah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Anas, from Anas:

When they suffered drought, ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, would seek rain through al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib. He would say, “O Allah, we used to seek a means to You through our Prophet, and You would give us rain. We seek a means to You through the uncle of our Prophet, so give us rain.” He said: They would be given rain.

Ishaq related to us. He said: Wahb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, from ‘Abbad ibn Tamim, from ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sought rain and turned his cloak.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr said that he heard ‘Abbad ibn Tamim relating to his father, from his uncle, ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to the prayer ground and sought rain. He faced the qibla, turned his cloak and prayed two units.

Abu ‘Abdullah said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah used to say that he was the one associated with the call to prayer, but he was mistaken, because this is ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn ‘Asim al-Mazini, from the Mazin of the Ansar.

Muhammad related to us. He said: Abu Damrah Anas ibn ‘Iyad informed us. He said: Sharik ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Namir related to us that he heard Anas ibn Malik mentioning:

A man entered on Friday through a door facing the pulpit while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing and delivering the sermon. He stood facing the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the livestock have perished and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to send us rain.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands and said, “O Allah, give us rain. O Allah, give us rain. O Allah, give us rain.”

Anas said: No, by Allah, we could see no cloud in the sky, not even a small patch, nor anything at all. There was no house or dwelling between us and Sal‘. He said: A cloud like a shield rose from behind it. When it reached the middle of the sky, it spread out and then rained.

He said: By Allah, we did not see the sun for six days. Then a man entered through that door on the following Friday while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing and delivering the sermon. He stood facing him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, property has been destroyed and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to hold it back.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, then said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us. O Allah, upon the high ground, the mountains, the thickets, the low hills, the valleys and the places where trees grow.” He said: It stopped, and we went out walking in the sunshine.

Sharik said: I asked Anas, “Was he the first man?” He said, “I do not know.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us, from Sharik, from Anas ibn Malik:

A man entered the mosque on a Friday through a door towards Dar al-Qada’ while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing and delivering the sermon. He stood facing the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then said, “O Messenger of Allah, property has been destroyed and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to send us rain.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, then said, “O Allah, come to our aid. O Allah, come to our aid. O Allah, come to our aid.”

Anas said: No, by Allah, we could see no cloud in the sky, not even a small patch. There was no house or dwelling between us and Sal‘. He said: A cloud like a shield rose from behind it. When it reached the middle of the sky, it spread out and then rained. No, by Allah, we did not see the sun for six days.

Then a man entered through that door on Friday—meaning the second Friday—while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing and delivering the sermon. He stood facing him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, property has been destroyed and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to hold it back from us.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, then said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us. O Allah, upon the high ground, the low hills, the valley bottoms and the places where trees grow.” He said: It ceased, and we went out walking in the sunshine.

Sharik said: I asked Anas ibn Malik, “Was he the first man?” He said, “I do not know.”

Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said:

While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon on Friday, a man came to him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the rain has failed, so supplicate to Allah to give us rain.” He supplicated, and rain fell upon us, so that we could hardly reach our homes. Rain continued to fall upon us until the following Friday. He said: That man, or someone else, stood up and said, “O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah to turn it away from us.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us.” He said: I saw the clouds breaking apart to the right and the left. They received rain, but the people of Medina did not.

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Sharik ibn ‘Abdullah, from Anas, who said:

A man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “The livestock have perished and the roads have been cut off.” He supplicated, and rain fell upon us from Friday to Friday. Then he came and said, “The houses have collapsed, the roads have been cut off and the livestock have perished, so supplicate to Allah to hold it back.” He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up and said, “O Allah, upon the high ground, the low hills, the valleys and the places where trees grow.” It cleared away from Medina as a garment is drawn off.

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Sharik ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Namir, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

A man came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the livestock have perished and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, supplicated, and they received rain from one Friday to the next. A man came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the houses have collapsed, the roads have been cut off and the livestock have perished.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “O Allah, upon the mountaintops, the high ground, the valley bottoms and the places where trees grow.” It cleared away from Medina as a garment is drawn off.

Al-Hasan ibn Bishr related to us. He said: Mu‘afa ibn ‘Imran related to us, from al-Awza‘i, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abdullah, from Anas ibn Malik:

A man complained to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, of the loss of property and the hardship of his dependants. He supplicated to Allah, seeking rain.

It was not mentioned that he turned his cloak or faced the qibla.

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Sharik ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Namir, from Anas ibn Malik:

A man came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the livestock have perished and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah.” He supplicated to Allah, and rain fell upon us from Friday to Friday. A man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the houses have collapsed, the roads have been cut off and the livestock have perished.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “O Allah, upon the backs of the mountains, the high ground, the valley bottoms and the places where trees grow.” It cleared away from Medina as a garment is drawn off.

Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us, from Sufyan: Mansur and al-A‘mash related to us, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said:

I went to Ibn Mas‘ud, and he said: Quraysh were slow to accept Islam, so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, supplicated against them. A year of scarcity overtook them, until they were perishing in it and ate carrion and bones. Abu Sufyan came to him and said, “O Muhammad, you came commanding that ties of kinship be maintained, and your people have perished, so supplicate to Allah.” He recited, “So watch for the day when the sky brings clear smoke.” Then they returned to their disbelief. That is His saying, Most High, “The day We strike the greatest blow”—the day of Badr.

Abu ‘Abdullah said: Asbat added, from Mansur:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, supplicated, and they were given rain. It covered them for seven days, and the people complained of the abundance of rain. He said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us.” The cloud moved down from above his head, and the people around them were given rain.

Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr related to us. Mu‘tamir related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah, from Thabit, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon on a Friday. The people stood up and cried out, saying, “O Messenger of Allah, the rain has failed, the trees have reddened and the animals have perished, so supplicate to Allah to give us rain.” He said, “O Allah, give us rain,” twice. By Allah, we could see no patch of cloud in the sky. A cloud formed and rained. He came down from the pulpit and prayed. When he had finished, it continued raining until the following Friday.

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood to deliver the sermon, they cried out to him, “The houses have collapsed and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to hold it back from us.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, smiled, then said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us.” It cleared away from Medina and began raining around it, while not a drop fell in Medina. I looked at Medina, and it was as though it were within a wreath.

And Abu Nu‘aym said to us, from Zuhayr, from Abu Ishaq:

‘Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Ansari went out, and al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib and Zayd ibn Arqam went out with him, may Allah Most High be pleased with them. He sought rain, standing on his feet before them, without a pulpit. He sought forgiveness, then prayed two rak‘ahs, reciting aloud. No adhan or iqamah was given.

Abu Ishaq said: ‘Abdullah ibn Yazid had seen the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Abbad ibn Tamim related to me that his uncle, who was one of the Companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, informed him:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out with the people to seek rain for them. He stood and supplicated to Allah while standing, then turned towards the qibla and turned his cloak, and they were given rain.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Abbad ibn Tamim, from his uncle, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to seek rain. He turned towards the qibla, supplicating, and turned his cloak. Then he prayed two rak‘ahs, reciting aloud in both.

Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Abbad ibn Tamim, from his uncle, who said:

I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on the day he went out to seek rain. He said: He turned his back to the people and faced the qibla, supplicating. Then he turned his cloak, then led us in two rak‘ahs, reciting aloud in both.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from ‘Abbad ibn Tamim, from his uncle:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sought rain, then prayed two rak‘ahs and reversed his cloak.

‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, who heard ‘Abbad ibn Tamim, from his uncle, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to the prayer ground to seek rain and faced the qibla. He prayed two rak‘ahs and reversed his cloak.

Sufyan said: Al-Mas‘udi informed me, from Abu Bakr, who said, “He put the right on the left.”

Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab informed us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad informed me that ‘Abbad ibn Tamim informed him that ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari informed him:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to the prayer ground to pray. When he supplicated, or intended to supplicate, he faced the qibla and turned his cloak.

Abu ‘Abdullah said: This Ibn Zayd is Mazini, and the earlier one is Kufi; he is Ibn Yazid.

Ayyub ibn Sulayman said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways related to me, from Sulayman ibn Bilal. Yahya ibn Sa‘id said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say:

A Bedouin man from the desert people came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on Friday and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the livestock have perished, the dependants have perished, the people have perished.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, supplicating, and the people raised their hands with him, supplicating.

He said: We had not left the mosque before rain fell upon us. Rain continued to fall upon us until the following Friday. The man came to the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the traveller is unable to proceed and the road is blocked.”

And al-Uwaysi said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far related to me, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id and Sharik, who both heard Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace,

that he raised his hands until I saw the whiteness of his armpits.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. Yahya and Ibn Abi ‘Adi related to us, from Sa‘id, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not raise his hands in any of his supplications except when seeking rain. He would raise them until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen.

Muhammad—he is Ibn Muqatil, Abu al-Hasan al-Marwazi—related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: ‘Ubaydullah informed us, from Nafi‘, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from ‘A’ishah:

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw rain, he would say, “May it be a beneficial downpour.”

Al-Qasim ibn Yahya corroborated it, from ‘Ubaydullah. Al-Awza‘i and ‘Uqayl also related it from Nafi‘.

Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Al-Awza‘i informed us. He said: Ishaq ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah al-Ansari related to us. He said: Anas ibn Malik related to me. He said:

The people were afflicted by a year of drought during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon on the pulpit on Friday, a Bedouin stood up and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the property has perished and the dependants have gone hungry. Supplicate to Allah for us to give us rain.”

He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, and there was not a small cloud in the sky. He said: Clouds like mountains rose up. He had not yet descended from his pulpit when I saw rain streaming down his beard.

He said: Rain fell upon us that day, the next day, the day after that and the following day, until the next Friday. That Bedouin, or another man, stood up and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the buildings have collapsed and the property has been submerged. Supplicate to Allah for us.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands and said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us.”

He said: Whenever he pointed with his hand towards a part of the sky, it cleared, until Madinah was like an open space. The valley—the valley of Qanat—flowed for a month. He said: No one came from any direction without speaking of the abundant rain.

Sa‘id ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far informed us. He said: Humayd informed me that he heard Anas say:

When a strong wind blew, that could be recognised in the face of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Muslim related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Abbas, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I was aided by al-Saba, and ‘Ad was destroyed by al-Dabur.”

Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us. He said: Abu al-Zinad informed us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The Hour will not come until knowledge is taken away, earthquakes become frequent, time draws close together, trials appear and harj increases”—and it is killing, killing—“until wealth becomes abundant among you and overflows.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Husayn ibn al-Hasan related to us. He said: Ibn ‘Awn related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said:

“O Allah, bless us in our Sham and in our Yemen.” He said: They said, “And in our Najd.” He said: He said, “O Allah, bless us in our Sham and in our Yemen.” He said: They said, “And in our Najd.” He said: He said, “There are earthquakes and trials there, and from there the horn of Satan rises.”

Isma‘il related to us. Malik related to me, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Mas‘ud, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in the dawn prayer at al-Hudaybiyah after rain during the night. When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished, he turned towards the people and said, “Do you know what your Lord said?” They said, “Allah and His messenger know best.”

He said, “Among My servants this morning are a believer in Me and a disbeliever. As for whoever said, ‘We were given rain by Allah’s favour and mercy,’ that person believes in Me and disbelieves in the star. But whoever said, ‘By the naw’ of such-and-such,’ that person disbelieves in Me and believes in the star.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The key to the unseen is five things that none knows except Allah: no one knows what will be tomorrow; no one knows what will be in the wombs; no soul knows what it will gain tomorrow; no soul knows in which land it will die; and no one knows when the rain will come.”

‘Amr ibn ‘Awn related to us. He said: Khalid related to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah, who said:

We were with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the sun was eclipsed. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up, dragging his cloak, until he entered the mosque. We entered, and he led us in two rak‘ahs until the sun became clear. Then he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The sun and the moon are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death. When you see them, pray and supplicate until what has befallen you is removed.”

Shihab ibn ‘Abbad related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Humayd related to us, from Isma‘il, from Qays, who said: I heard Abu Mas‘ud saying:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The sun and the moon are not eclipsed because of the death of any person. They are, however, two of Allah’s signs. When you see them, stand up and pray.”

Asbagh related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb informed me. He said: ‘Amr informed me, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, who related it to him, from his father, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who used to report from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“The sun and the moon are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. They are, however, two of Allah’s signs. When you see them, pray.”

‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us. He said: Shayban Abu Mu‘awiyah related to us, from Ziyad ibn ‘Ilaqah, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah, who said:

The sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on the day Ibrahim died. The people said: “The sun was eclipsed because of Ibrahim’s death.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The sun and the moon are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. When you see this, pray and supplicate to Allah.”

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘Aishah, who said:

The sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led the people in prayer. He stood and prolonged the standing, then bowed and prolonged the bowing. Then he stood and prolonged the standing, but it was shorter than the first standing. Then he bowed and prolonged the bowing, but it was shorter than the first bowing. Then he prostrated and prolonged the prostration. Then he did in the second rak‘ah as he had done in the first. Then he finished, and the sun had cleared. He addressed the people, praised Allah and extolled Him.

Then he said: “The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. When you see this, supplicate to Allah, proclaim His greatness, pray and give charity.”

Then he said: “O community of Muhammad, by Allah, no one has greater ghayrah than Allah concerning His male servant committing unlawful sexual intercourse or His female servant committing unlawful sexual intercourse. O community of Muhammad, by Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much.”

Ishaq related to me. He said: Yahya ibn Salih informed us. He said: Mu‘awiyah ibn Sallam ibn Abi Sallam al-Habashi al-Dimashqi related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us. He said: Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf al-Zuhri informed me, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

When the sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the announcement was made: “The prayer is in congregation.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: al-Layth related to me, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab.

Another chain: Ahmad ibn Salih related to me. He said: ‘Anbasah related to us. He said: Yunus related to us, from Ibn Shihab: ‘Urwah related to me, from ‘Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

The sun was eclipsed during the life of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He went out to the mosque, and the people formed rows behind him. He proclaimed Allah’s greatness, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited at length. Then he proclaimed Allah’s greatness and bowed for a long time. Then he said: “Allah hears whoever praises Him.” He stood and did not prostrate, and recited at length, but less than the first recitation. Then he proclaimed Allah’s greatness and bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he said: “Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, to You belongs praise.” Then he prostrated. Then he said the like of that in the other rak‘ah, completing four bowings in four prostrations. The sun cleared before he finished.

Then he stood and praised Allah as He deserves. Then he said: “They are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. When you see them, hasten to prayer.”

Kathir ibn ‘Abbas used to relate that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, used to relate an account of the day the sun was eclipsed like ‘Urwah’s report from ‘Aishah. I said to ‘Urwah: “On the day it was eclipsed in Madinah, your brother did not pray more than two rak‘ahs, like the dawn prayer.” He said: “Yes, because he was mistaken about the Sunnah.”

Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr related to us. He said: al-Layth related to us: ‘Uqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, informed him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed on the day the sun was eclipsed. He stood and proclaimed Allah’s greatness, and recited at length. Then he bowed for a long time. Then he raised his head and said: “Allah hears whoever praises Him.” He remained standing as he was. Then he recited at length, but less than the first recitation. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he prostrated for a long time. Then he did the like of that in the other rak‘ah. Then he gave the greeting of peace, and the sun had cleared.

He addressed the people and said concerning the eclipse of the sun and the moon: “They are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. When you see them, hasten to prayer.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death, but Allah Most High makes His servants fear through them.”

Abu ‘Abdullah said: ‘Abd al-Warith, Shu‘bah, Khalid ibn ‘Abdullah and Hammad ibn Salamah did not mention, from Yunus, “makes His servants fear through them.” Musa followed him in transmitting it, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, who said: Abu Bakrah informed me, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Allah Most High makes His servants fear through them.” Ash‘ath followed him in transmitting it, from al-Hasan.

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Amrah bint ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

A Jewish woman came to ask her, and said to her: “May Allah protect you from the punishment of the grave.” ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Are people punished in their graves?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I seek refuge in Allah from that.”

Then one morning the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went riding, and the sun was eclipsed. He returned in the forenoon. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed among the chambers. Then he stood to pray, and the people stood behind him.

He stood for a long time, then bowed for a long time. Then he rose and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he rose and prostrated. Then he stood, and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he rose and prostrated. He finished and said what Allah willed him to say. Then he instructed them to seek refuge from the punishment of the grave.

Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, who said:

When the sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the announcement was made: “The prayer is in congregation.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed two bowings in one rak‘ah. Then he stood and performed two bowings in one rak‘ah. Then he sat down. Then the sun cleared.

He said: ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, said: “I have never made a prostration longer than that.”

‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed. He stood for a long time, about as long as the recitation of Surat al-Baqarah. Then he bowed for a long time. Then he rose and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he prostrated. Then he stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he rose and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he prostrated. Then he finished, and the sun had cleared.

Then he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. When you see that, remember Allah.”

They said: “Messenger of Allah, we saw you reach for something where you stood, then we saw you draw back.” He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw Paradise and reached for a cluster. Had I taken it, you would have eaten from it for as long as the world remains. I was shown the Fire, and I have never seen a sight more dreadful than today’s. I saw that most of its inhabitants were women.”

They said: “Why, Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Because of their ingratitude.” It was said: “Do they disbelieve in Allah?” He said: “They are ungrateful to their husbands and ungrateful for kindness. If you were kind to one of them for all time, then she saw something from you, she would say: ‘I have never seen any good from you.’”

‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his wife Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, from Asma’ bint Abi Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

I came to ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the sun was eclipsed. The people were standing in prayer, and she was standing in prayer. I said: “What is happening with the people?” She pointed with her hand toward the sky and said: “Glory be to Allah.” I said: “A sign?” She indicated: yes. She said: I stood until faintness overcame me, and I began pouring water over my head. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished, he praised Allah and extolled Him.

Then he said: “There is nothing I had not seen before but that I have seen it while standing here, even Paradise and the Fire. It has been revealed to me that you will be tested in the graves with a trial like, or close to, the trial of the Dajjal—

I do not know which of the two Asma’ said.

one of you will be approached and asked: ‘What do you know of this man?’ As for the believer, or the one who is certain—

I do not know which of those Asma’ said.

he will say: ‘Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to us with clear proofs and guidance. We responded, believed and followed.’ It will be said to him: ‘Sleep in peace; we have known that you were indeed certain.’ As for the hypocrite, or the one who doubts—

I do not know which of the two Asma’ said.

he will say: ‘I do not know. I heard people saying something, so I said it.’”

Rabi‘ ibn Yahya related to us. He said: Za’idah related to us, from Hisham, from Fatimah, from Asma’, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, indeed commanded the freeing of slaves during a solar eclipse.

Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Amrah bint ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

A Jewish woman came to ask her, and said: “May Allah protect you from the punishment of the grave.” ‘Aishah asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Are people punished in their graves?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I seek refuge in Allah from that.”

Then one morning the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went riding, and the sun was eclipsed. He returned in the forenoon. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed among the chambers. Then he stood and prayed, and the people stood behind him.

He stood for a long time, then bowed for a long time. Then he rose and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he rose and prostrated for a long time. Then he stood, and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he prostrated, but less than the first prostration.

Then he finished, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said what Allah willed him to say. Then he instructed them to seek refuge from the punishment of the grave.

Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Isma‘il, who said: Qays related to me, from Abu Mas‘ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The sun and the moon are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. They are, however, two of Allah’s signs. When you see them, pray.”

‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri and Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from ‘Urwah, from ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

The sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood and led the people in prayer. He prolonged the recitation. Then he bowed and prolonged the bowing. Then he raised his head and prolonged the recitation, but it was less than his first recitation. Then he bowed and prolonged the bowing, but less than his first bowing. Then he raised his head and prostrated twice. Then he stood and did the like of that in the second rak‘ah.

Then he stood and said: “The sun and the moon are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. They are, however, two of Allah’s signs which He shows His servants. When you see that, hasten to prayer.”

Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Burayd ibn ‘Abdullah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said:

The sun was eclipsed, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up in alarm, fearing that it might be the Hour. He came to the mosque and prayed with the longest standing, bowing and prostration I had ever seen him perform.

He said: “These signs which Allah sends do not occur because of anyone’s death or life, but {Allah makes His servants fear through them}. When you see anything of that, hasten to remember Him, supplicate to Him and seek His forgiveness.”
